P01-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: the book opens on two datelines in two counting systems - בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.1.1, a regnal/exilic year the book never names an era for) and הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין (oshb:Ezek.1.2, the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile) - followed at oshb:Ezek.1.3 by the superscription הָיֹ֣ה הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְ֠הוָה אֶל יְחֶזְקֵ֨אל, an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect word-event with a THIRD-PERSON addressee ('to Ezekiel', not 'to me'). This verb and addressee shape are why the verse sits in the 49-verse any-form word-event count and not the 48-verse first-person family (sweep: verses containing the word-event phrase in any form, 49; the 48 excludes this one verse by predicate). It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The same verse also carries וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָֽה, the hand-of-YHWH construct that opens the book's first vision (one of 7 verses carrying the construct). Close: the scene runs unbroken to oshb:Ezek.1.28, מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר, glossed by the WEB as “This was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh’s glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke” (web:Ezek.1.28). No word-event, messenger, recognition or utterance formula interrupts 1:4-1:27 (the transport-verb and 'he said to me' sweeps that mark scene changes elsewhere in the book's visions do not begin until chapter 8), so the throne-theophany carries no formula-marked internal seam; the samekh recorded after 1:28 and the fresh 'he said to me' that opens oshb:Ezek.2.1 together mark the vision/commission seam on the FAR side of this unit; the onset evidence at oshb:Ezek.2.1 is weighed there. The reduced confidence rests on this close, as measured on the witness: 1:28 ends the theophany on a narrative turn, the prophet falling on his face and hearing a voice, with no close-role formula in the verse, so its near face is a discernible close without a counted device, and the samekh recorded after it (single-witness) corroborates that close without deciding it.
P01-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating oshb:Ezek.1.1-1.3 as its own superscription unit, separate from the vision it introduces. Rejected because the vision proper (1:4-1:28) carries no independent onset device of its own - it simply continues the sentence the hand-of-YHWH clause opens - so cutting after 1:3 would manufacture a seam the bytes do not mark, and would still leave a 25-verse remainder.
P01-001.device_notes: Length disclosed as a fact: a whole-chapter span of 28 verses against the target of 7-10 verses per row; the length is no ground for the grade, and no internal cut is forced where the bytes mark none. MT 1:3 is cited only under the 49-verse any-form word-event count, never blended with the 48-verse first-person family. K/Q at 1:8 checked before quoting: the unit does not splice the disputed word. The OSHB editorial note at 1:11 is disclosed as single-witness apparatus, not a reading change. Paseq at 1:1 and 1:27 disclosed count-only (single-witness); no intra-verse position is claimed.

P01-007.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:22 וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.3.22) (“Yahweh’s hand was there on me” (web:Ezek.3.22)), the hand-of-YHWH construct read here as a genuine vision onset (contrast oshb:Ezek.3.14, where the construct accompanies the spirit carrying the prophet away, a transit rather than a new scene) because it opens a fresh scene: “Arise, go out into the plain” (web:Ezek.3.22). 3:25 announces that עֲבוֹתִ֔ים (oshb:Ezek.3.25) ('ropes') will be put on the prophet; the word recurs at 4:8 in the siege sign-act, across the 3:27/4:1 seam (the same consonants and vowels under a different accent), so the muteness command and the sign-acts share a device, and that continuity is weighed here against the seam even though the unit boundary stands. 3:26 carries the fifth rebellious-house refrain, כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה. Close: 3:27, הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.3.27) (“He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house” (web:Ezek.3.27)) - the sixth verse in chapters 2-3 to name the rebellious house (sweep: 12 verses book-wide name it, six of them in chapters 2-3), and the close of the book's opening collection (chapters 1-3); a samekh is recorded after this verse. Across the seam, 4:1 opens with וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.1) ('and you, son of man'), quoted byte for byte as the 3:27 clause is, and turns to the command to take a tile, the sub-onset that starts the sign-acts. The unit therefore stops at 3:27 and does not extend into 4:1; the seam's near side is closed by the refrain and the samekh after 3:27 (single witness), and its far side is opened by that sub-onset.
P01-007.strongest_rejected_alternative: Placing the seam between the book's first two collections at 3:15/3:16 instead of 3:27/4:1, on the strength of 3:16's own strict word-event and the seven-day close it answers. Weighed on the bytes, the onset side of that seam is strong: 3:16 sets מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16)) before its strict word-event, and a pe follows 3:16 itself (single witness), after the word-event verse rather than before it. Its close side is narrative: 3:15 ends the journey to the exiles on seven days of sitting among them, a report rather than a refrain. The rebellious-house refrain runs on both sides of 3:16 (sweep: of the six verses in chapters 2-3 that name the rebellious house, four stand before 3:16 and two after it), so a parent seam there would divide that series, whereas at 3:27/4:1 the series' sixth verse stands on the close side and the sub-onset of 4:1 on the onset side. The alternative is kept as a held question and not argued away, because the ropes of 3:25, taken up at 4:8, tie the muteness command (3:22-27) to the sign-acts (4:1-17) across the later seam.
P01-007.device_notes: Category deviation disclosed: this span also reads as a commission narrative (the muteness charge proper runs 3:24-3:27 inside this vision-opened scene); it is classed with the vision reports because the unit's onset device is the hand-of-YHWH construct at 3:22. Paseq at 3:27 occurs twice (double occurrence on one verse), disclosed count-only, single-witness. The ropes word shared by 3:25 and 4:8 is disclosed as continuity across the 3:27/4:1 seam; it argues for the closeness of the two units, while the refrain close at 3:27 and the sub-onset at 4:1 keep the seam between them. The witness records a samekh after MT 3:21 (single witness), on the far side of this unit's onset seam, where it corroborates the onset without deciding it.

P01-012.boundary_rationale: Onset: 7:1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.7.1) (“Moreover Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.7.1)), a strict word-event textually identical to 6:1's formula, a hard seam. Close: 7:4, וִידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.7.4) (“Then you will know that I am Yahweh” (web:Ezek.7.4)), the 2mp wider-family recognition close, with a pe recorded after it, before 7:5 reopens with a fresh messenger formula on the same 'end' theme. Measured on the witness, each seam carries a signal on both faces: the word-event of 7:1 follows 6:14, which ends verse-final on the recognition formula with a pe recorded after it (single-witness), and the verse-final recognition of 7:4, with its own pe, stands before the messenger formula of 7:5; on those faces the row would stand higher, and it is held at reduced confidence because how chapter 7 divides, 7:1-4 against 7:5-27, is a standing open question.

P02-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating all of 10:1-17 (the errand plus the wheel description) as one row was weighed, since nothing but content separates them. It was not taken because 10:9-17 is a self-contained descriptive unit in its own right and folding it in here would produce a seventeen-verse row (MEASURED: web:Ezek.10.1-Ezek.10.17 runs to 17 verses, counted verse by verse on its WEB face) with no formula, transport verb or parashah mark inside it to seat a seam, in a chapter that carries no mark at all (single-witness).

P03-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Classifying 16:59-63 as the close of the chapter's extended allegory rather than as a separate restoration-promise row was weighed and not taken: the covenant-establishment promise ('I will establish for you an everlasting covenant') is a restoration burden distinct in kind from the accusation and sentence that fill the rest of the chapter, and it opens with its own messenger formula rather than continuing the sisters comparison; that deviation from the chapter's otherwise uniform category is disclosed here.
P03-009.device_notes: Category deviation disclosed: this row is typed as a restoration promise rather than as part of the allegory, although it sits inside MT 16, because the covenant-establishment promise opening at 16:59 carries its own messenger formula and turns from the sisters' indictment to YHWH's remembered covenant, so this restoration burden is cut off from the accusation that precedes it. MT 16:59 Ketiv/Qere single note disclosed above. A samekh is set after MT 16:58 (single witness); that front-seam break divides the sisters' sentence from the covenant turn this row opens. Measured on the witness, both seams carry a signal on each face: the messenger formula of 16:59 follows 16:58, which ends verse-final on the utterance formula with that samekh after it, and the verse-final utterance formula of 16:63, with a samekh after it, stands before the strict word-event that opens 17:1; the faces by themselves would carry more, and the row stays at reduced confidence because whether 16:59-63 stands as a restoration promise of its own or as the allegory's close remains an open question.

P03-015.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:5 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְאִ֖ישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.5) ('if a man is righteous and does what is just and right'), a default case-law onset following the thesis stated at 18:4; the samekh recorded there (single-witness), closing the unit before it, corroborates this row's onset from the far side of the seam. Close side: the row runs to 18:9, and its own final words are the utterance formula חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.9), a genuine verse-final refrain closing the first case before the wicked son's case opens at 18:10 with no formula of its own. That utterance is verse-final and carries no mark, and 18:10 brings no fresh onset past it, so it closes a paragraph inside the one word-event unit and not the unit itself. Behind 18:5 the seam is a case turn with no formula on either face, corroborated by the samekh on 18:4 and not decided by it. The two seams differ in shape, and the onset seam is the weaker: measured on the witness, its near face carries no device at all and its far face ends on the thesis without a close formula, which is what holds the row at reduced confidence; the close seam’s near face at least ends on the utterance formula, though nothing answers it at 18:10.
P03-015.strongest_rejected_alternative: No parashah mark (single-witness) corroborates a seam at 18:9; keeping 18:5-9 fused with 18:10-20 into one eleven-plus-five-verse row was weighed and not taken because the utterance formula at 18:9 is genuinely verse-final and so marks the one formula-marked seam inside the chapter’s case law, unlike its four non-final recurrences elsewhere in MT 18 (18:3, 18:23, 18:30, 18:32). That signature is paragraph-final where it stands, since 18:10 brings no fresh onset past it, so the ground for refusing the fusion is a paragraph-grade signal and no more; the seam is kept as a case turn inside one word-event unit, and that paragraph-grade footing is part of why the row stands at reduced confidence.
P03-015.device_notes: No K/Q note, no paseq, no parashah mark, and no editorial note lie within this span (single-witness).

P06-002.device_notes: 25:9 carries a K/Q note (place name, ketiv/qere pair, morpheme separators stripped: ketiv וקריתמה / Qere וְקִרְיָתָֽיְמָה, oshb:Ezek.25.9, K/Q, ketiv/qere); disclosed, not used to argue a boundary. Recognition close at 25:11 is the strict 28-verse 3mp form, cited as such and never blended with the wider 2mp family used at Ezek.25.5. Measured on the witness, each seam carries a signal on both faces: the messenger formula of 25:8, turning the address to Moab and Seir, follows 25:7, which ends verse-final on the recognition formula with a samekh after it (single-witness), and the verse-final recognition of 25:11, with its own samekh, stands before the messenger formula of 25:12 that turns to Edom; the faces would bear a higher grade, and the row is kept at reduced confidence because how chapter 25 tiles its four short oracles, as four rows or two or one, is held open as a question.

P06-014.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:20 is the strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.28.20), and 28:21 names the fresh addressee in the command “set your face toward Sidon, and prophesy against it” (web:Ezek.28.21). The far face of that seam carries no signal: 28:19 ends on the Tyre dirge’s refrain, בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔יתָ וְאֵינְךָ֖ עַד עוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.28.19), and carries a pe (single-witness); neither is a counted close formula. Close: 28:23 ends verse-final on the recognition formula וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.28.23), counted in its strict form, with no mark after it, and the far face is empty here as well, for 28:24 opens וְלֹֽא יִהְיֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Ezek.28.24) with no onset device and turns the promise toward Israel. Measured on the witness, each seam carries a licensed signal on its near face only, and that is the ground on which the row stands one step below the top grade. Inside the span, the messenger formula of 28:22 is paragraph-grade: it opens the speech that 28:21 commands the prophet to deliver (וְאָמַרְתָּ֗, 'and say', oshb:Ezek.28.22), and Sidon is the one addressed on both sides of it (a reading of the command’s wording).
P06-014.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the Israel coda of 28:24-26 inside the Sidon oracle, so that one unit runs from the word-event of 28:20 to the close of 28:26. The coda carries no word-event of its own and 28:24 opens with no onset device, so on the bytes alone the seam after 28:23 rests on its near face. It is not taken because 28:24-26 stands apart by verse as a restoration coda addressed to Israel inside the collection against the nations, a unit of its own in the book’s division, and because 28:23 closes the Sidon oracle on its own verse-final recognition before the address turns.
P06-014.device_notes: Two interior candidate seams are weighed and not taken. At 28:21/28:22 the messenger formula follows a command verse that ends on no close-role formula and delivers the speech that command orders, so it marks a paragraph. At 28:22/28:23 the recognition formula of 28:22 stands inside its verse, with the clauses of executed judgment and sanctification after it, and 28:23 opens with no onset device, so no seam is carried there. No K/Q note, editors’ note, paseq or parashah mark falls inside 28:20-23 (single-witness); the pe recorded after 28:19 stands behind the onset, and the samekh recorded after 28:24 falls inside the coda, not at this close.

P07-001.boundary_rationale: Onset side: the hard-seam dateline at oshb:Ezek.29.1 (year 10, month 10, day 12) uses the perfect hayah word-event form, immediately followed by the set-your-face address to Pharaoh at oshb:Ezek.29.2 and the messenger formula opening the verdict speech at oshb:Ezek.29.3 (the great-monster-in-his-rivers charge). Close side: the strict recognition formula at oshb:Ezek.29.9a closes the crocodile-verdict unit; the same verse continues with a causal clause the WEB itself paragraphs mid-verse (web:Ezek.29.9), and oshb:Ezek.29.10 opens a fresh against-you verdict cycle restating the same charge -- an onset/close collision at 29:9 -> 29:10 -- so the row seam sits at the verse boundary after 29:9, not inside it. Measured on the witness, that close is the weak mid-verse shape: the recognition formula runs only to the etnachta, and an independent causal clause with its own finite verb, יַ֧עַן אָמַ֛ר (oshb:Ezek.29.9), fills the rest of the verse; this mid-verse close is the ground on which the row is held at reduced confidence.
P07-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: Three alternatives are weighed. (1) Ending the row at 29:6, where an extended (non-strict) recognition-type close occurs; rejected because 29:7 continues the same staff-of-reed image with no intervening onset, and because this chapter's own onset/close collision pattern places the true seam after 29:9, not 29:6. Two further readings are weighed. (2) Cutting at 29:7/29:8 - the alternative the paragraph layer proposes, and the witness's sectioning is disclosed for it: MEASURED, this witness places a SAMEKH (setumah, closed section, single-witness) after MT 29:7, recorded on the verse it follows, and that verse additionally carries one ketiv/qere pair, already disclosed in this row. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 29:8 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.29.8), and with it a grammatical addressee shift - MT 29:7 addresses a masculine singular and MT 29:8 a feminine singular (oshb:Ezek.29.7, oshb:Ezek.29.8), that is, from Pharaoh to the land. Whether it is licensed: a messenger formula cuts as a sub-onset when its addressee differs from the one before or when the preceding verse ends on a close-role formula, and the first of those IS satisfied by that addressee change, so this rival is licensed and is not dismissed. It is one-faced: MT 29:7 ends with no close-role formula, so the second would fail there, and the SAMEKH after it (single-witness) is a mark, which makes no face. The stated ground on which this row holds: the crocodile verdict's own refrain is the recognition formula at MT 29:9, and MT 29:10 restates the same charge as a fresh against-you cycle (oshb:Ezek.29.10); since a licensed text signal takes precedence over a section mark, the SAMEKH after MT 29:7 is weak corroboration, disclosed FOR this rival and not for this row. (3) Tiling MT 29:1-29:16 as ONE row, with the mid-verse WEB paragraph at 29:9 and the forty-years turn at 29:13 falling inside it. What supports it: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, no dateline and no word-event formula stands anywhere between MT 29:1 and the next dateline at MT 29:17; MEASURED in this witness, the marks inside that stretch follow MT 29:7 (a samekh) and MT 29:12 (a pe), a further pe follows MT 29:16 at that stretch's own close and corroborates this alternative, and NO mark stands on MT 29:9 (single-witness). And this row's own close has the weak mid-verse shape: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the recognition formula in MT 29:9 ends at the etnachta and an INDEPENDENT causal clause with a finite verb fills the rest of the verse (oshb:Ezek.29.9) - unlike MT 29:6, whose words after its own recognition clause are a causal phrase built on an infinitive construct (oshb:Ezek.29.6), a dependent completion that grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal rather than the weak mid-verse shape. The stated ground on which this row holds: MT 29:10 opens a fresh against-you verdict cycle restating the charge, so the collision is resolved at the verse boundary after 29:9. The weakness of the 29:9 close and the case for a single 29:1-16 row are disclosed rather than argued away; the mid-verse close at 29:9 is the ground for the row's reduced confidence.

P07-006.boundary_rationale: Onset side: the hard-seam dateline at oshb:Ezek.31.1 (year 11, month 3, day 1, perfect hayah word-event form) opens onto the son-of-man command at oshb:Ezek.31.2, a rhetorical-comparison opening ('whom are you like') that runs the full cedar figure (31:3-9), its verdict via the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.31.10, its felling (31:11-14), and its descent to Sheol via the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.31.15. Close side: the unit ends at oshb:Ezek.31.18 with the explicit identification of the cedar as Pharaoh and the utterance formula, immediately before the hard-seam dateline at 32:1. The two internal messenger-formula recurrences (31:10, 31:15) keep the same addressee/figure throughout and neither is preceded by a refrain close, so neither licenses a row cut, and the whole eighteen-verse allegory is held as one row, its length disclosed. Measured on the witness, both seams carry signals on both faces: the verse-final recognition that ends 30:26 stands behind the 31:1 dateline, and the verse-final utterance of 31:18 stands before the 32:1 dateline. The reduced confidence therefore does not come from the faces; it rests on a standing open question about the chapter, which is one cedar allegory under a dateline whose category, oracle against a nation or allegory, is left unresolved.
P07-006.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 31:9/31:10 (figure versus verdict) or 31:14/31:15 (verdict versus Sheol descent); both rejected because neither messenger-formula recurrence changes addressee and neither is preceded by a refrain close, so they mark paragraphs, not rows; the genre itself is held between an oracle against a nation and an extended allegory, disclosed rather than resolved.
P07-006.device_notes: Length disclosed as a fact: a whole-chapter span of 18 verses, against the target of 7-10 verses per row; the length is no ground for the grade. K/Q at oshb:Ezek.31.5; single-witness samekh follows oshb:Ezek.31.9, oshb:Ezek.31.14 and oshb:Ezek.31.18; the closing verse oshb:Ezek.31.18 also carries two OSHB editorial notes (an accent divergence from BHS and a ketiv/qere divergence from BHS), single-witness apparatus, disclosed. Genre held between an oracle against a nation (the messenger-formula verdict structure) and an allegory (the extended whom-are-you-like figure); typed here in the oracle-against-nation category, the deviation from the figure's own category disclosed rather than silently resolved. P08-016.boundary_rationale: Onset: 36:1 opens וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.36.1), “You, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel” (web:Ezek.36.1), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset with the address turning from Mount Seir to Israel’s mountains; the verse behind it, 35:15, ends verse-final on the recognition formula וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.35.15), with a pe recorded after it (single-witness), so both faces of the seam carry a signal. The sub-onset stands inside the word-event unit that opens at 35:1, whose frame this oracle shares with the oracle against Mount Seir in 35:1-15, and that shared frame is disclosed. Close: 36:15 ends verse-final on נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.15; the verse’s K/Q note, ketiv and qere, falls on another word) with a samekh recorded after it (single-witness), and 36:16 opens on the strict word-event formula (oshb:Ezek.36.16), so this seam too is signalled on both faces. Measured on the witness, the faces alone would carry the row higher; it is held at reduced confidence because 35:1-36:15 is one word-event unit running across the chapter break, and whether that unit divides at 36:1 is a standing open question. Inside the span, the messenger chain of 36:2-7 and the turns after 36:11 and at 36:13 mark paragraphs rather than units, as the device notes set out.
P08-016.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 35:1-36:15 as one row, the single word-event unit that runs across the chapter break, with the oracle against Mount Seir and the oracle to Israel’s mountains under the one formula of 35:1. Weighed and not taken: 36:1 opens on 'and you, son of man' with the address turning from Seir to the mountains, after 35:15 has ended verse-final on the recognition formula with a pe recorded after it (single-witness), so the sub-onset is licensed and both of its faces carry a signal. The shared frame is disclosed rather than hidden, and the open question of the larger unit is what keeps this row at reduced confidence.
P08-016.device_notes: Interior seams weighed and not taken: the messenger formulae that stand in each verse of 36:2-7 run as one chain of paragraphs, and the samekh recorded after 36:4 (single-witness) corroborates a paragraph there without deciding a seam; 36:11 ends verse-final on the recognition formula, but 36:12 opens with no onset device; 36:13’s messenger formula follows 36:12, which ends on no close-role formula and has only a samekh recorded after it, and the land stays the one addressed: the address shifts toward the land in the feminine singular from 36:13, a verse that still carries a masculine-plural 'to you' (לָכֶ֔ם, oshb:Ezek.36.13), so the referent does not change (a reading on measured bytes). Five K/Q notes fall inside the span, two at 36:13, two at 36:14 and one at 36:15, their ketiv and qere forms listed with the references (single-witness apparatus); none is argued for a boundary. Paseq is recorded once within 36:5 and once within 36:6 (count-only, single-witness); the position of either stroke within its verse is not stated. An editors’ note on the accents stands at 36:7 (single-witness apparatus), disclosed and not argued. The row’s burden is the restoration of the mountains, their tilling, sowing and resettlement, and the end of the nations’ taunt against the land, which places it among the restoration promises rather than the oracles against foreign nations, though it shares the frame of 35:1 with the Seir oracle. Length disclosed as a fact: 15 verses, against the target of 7-10 verses per row.

P09-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: the verse opens on the hand-of-YHWH idiom immediately followed by a transport verb, oshb:Ezek.37.1 הָיְתָ֣ה עָלַי֮ יַד יְהוָה֒ וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נִי בְר֨וּחַ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְנִיחֵ֖נִי בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבִּקְעָ֑ה וְהִ֖יא מְלֵאָ֥ה עֲצָמֽוֹת -- the same onset shape that opens the book's other three long prose visions, and this occurrence is one of only 7 hand-of-YHWH verses in the book. The unit is held as one scene, with the live rival inside it weighed below: the prophet is set down among the bones (37.1-2), questioned and commanded to prophesy twice -- once to the bones, once to the breath/spirit (37.4-6, 37.9), watches the two-stage reanimation (37.7-8, 37.10), and receives the scene's own interpretation as a word to 'son of man' (oshb:Ezek.37.11 וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ). Close: oshb:Ezek.37.14 stacks three refrain-grade closes in one verse -- the second-person plural recognition variant (the knowing clause addressed to the hearers in the plural, part of a 21-verse 2mp family sweep), the emphatic 'I YHWH have spoken' close (one of 14 book-wide), and the short utterance signature without the divine-name pair (one of only 4 such short forms in the book) -- וְנָתַתִּ֨י רוּחִ֤י בָכֶם֙ וִחְיִיתֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל אַדְמַתְכֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֞ם כִּי אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִׂ֖יתִי נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, and a pe mark is recorded immediately after this verse (single-witness, informing not deciding). Both sides of the following seam were weighed: oshb:Ezek.37.15 opens with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, one of 39 verses carrying that strict form, so the close at 37.14 and the fresh onset at 37.15 corroborate each other from both directions. Both faces of that close are top grade; measured on the witness, the row stands one step below the top grade because a licensed rival lies inside the span, at the 37.10/37.11 seam.
P09-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split at the two samekh-marked points inside the scene: after the army stands up at oshb:Ezek.37.10, and after the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.37.12 (single-witness marks on both). The first is a real and licensed rival: 37.11 opens on a he-said-to-me clause with the son-of-man address (sweep: 93 verses book-wide), a default onset inside a vision, with the samekh standing behind it on 37.10 -- so 37.1-10 would be a complete scene (the question, the command to prophesy, and the army that stands up as its result) and 37.11-14 its interpretation, which carries a messenger formula of its own at 37.12 and a recognition close. It is not taken because 37.1-14 is held as one vision scene. The other he-said-to-me verses inside it (37.3, 37.4, 37.9) are onset-type devices inside the vision and each is a licensed alternative; they are held because the question, the two commands and their two results form one scene, taken whole as the vision of the bones, and the transport at 37.2 would leave a one-verse remainder. The 37.10/37.11 rival remains the one that keeps the grade short of the top; which of the recognition clauses at 37.6, 37.13 and 37.14 closes the row is held open here.
P09-001.device_notes: 37.2 and 37.9 each carry one paseq (count-only, single-witness; the count is taken verse by verse from this witness's paseq apparatus, so no position inside either verse is claimed). 37.9 also carries an OSHB editorial note recording an accent divergence from BHS (single-witness apparatus, not a text variant). The WEB prints a mid-verse paragraph inside 37.3 (“Son of man, can these bones live?” (web:Ezek.37.3), then the prophet's reply) -- texture, cited only and never a boundary argument. The witness also records a samekh after MT 36:38 (single witness), the paragraph mark behind this row's onset. The second-person plural recognition variant stands inside the scene at 37.6 as well as at the close, disclosed here and arguing no boundary. The he-said-to-me verses weighed as licensed onsets and not taken are 37.3 (a cut there would leave 37.1-2 as a two-verse remainder, too short to stand as a unit of its own), 37.4 (the command answers the question of 37.3 inside one exchange) and 37.9 (the second command answers the result of the first stage and leaves the scene incomplete).

P09-007.device_notes: Held at the lowest confidence because the recapitulation-versus-sequence question that runs through the Gog chapters sits on this row's own onset: 39.1-3 repeats 38.3's verdict against Gog almost word for word, and no position is taken here on whether that repetition restarts the oracle's own movement or advances it -- both readings remain live on these bytes. The faces alone would carry more: the onset follows the verse-final recognition formula of 38.23 with a samekh after it, and the close is the verse-final utterance formula of 39.10 with a samekh after it (single witness for both marks), though 39.11 opens with no onset device; it is the open question at the onset, stated here as the row's own ground, that holds the row at the lowest grade. 39.9 carries one paseq (count-only, single-witness) inside this span.

P09-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: no word-event, messenger, hand-of-YHWH or address formula opens 39:21, whose near face therefore carries no device of any tracked class, and the single witness records no mark at 39:20 either; the seam rests on the verse-final utterance signature at 39:20, which stands there alone, and on the topical turn from the birds-and-beasts summons to a first-person retrospective on Israel's exile. Inside that retrospective the wide-family recognition close addressed to “the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.39.22) stands at 39.22, one of the expansions in the 64-verse wide sweep and not the strict 28, and is internal, paragraph-final rather than row-final; 39.23 is no second such close -- its knowing-clause carries no divine-name predicate and belongs to no tracked class. The onset at 39:21 is thus a topical turn without any onset device, and the Gog chapters 38-39, where recapitulation and sequence remain an open question, are held at reduced confidence as a stretch; both are the ground for the confidence this row carries. Close: 39.21-24 ends at oshb:Ezek.39.24 כְּטֻמְאָתָ֥ם וּכְפִשְׁעֵיהֶ֖ם עָשִׂ֣יתִי אֹתָ֑ם וָאַסְתִּ֥ר פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶֽם, with a samekh mark recorded immediately after (single-witness); 39.25 then reopens with a fresh messenger formula, weighed from the far side of the seam.
P09-010.device_notes: The clause “I hid my face from them” (web:Ezek.39.24, and again at web:Ezek.39.23), in this witness וָאַסְתִּ֥ר פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.39.24), recurs almost verbatim at 39.29 (“I won’t hide my face from them any more” (web:Ezek.39.29)), a byte-true device that straddles the 39.21-24 close and the 39.25-29 onset; it is disclosed here as continuity texture rather than treated as counterevidence against the samekh-marked seam at 39.24, since the second occurrence is explicitly negated and paired with a fresh messenger formula at 39.25, not a bare repetition.

P10-013.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:10 opens אַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.43.10) 'you, son of man' directly after the samekh (single-witness) closing at oshb:Ezek.43.9 -- a near-form of the book's twenty-three-verse 'and you, son of man' sub-onset family, here without the leading vav, disclosed as such rather than counted against that sweep. It charges the prophet to show the house's pattern so Israel may be ashamed of its iniquities. Close side: 43:12 closes on a doubled envelope formula, זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת ... הִנֵּה זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.43.12) “This is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12) ... “Behold, this is the law of the house” (web:Ezek.43.12), repeating the title at the top and bottom of the same verse -- a strong lexical close-device, and the reason this three-verse span is held as its own row despite its length: the inclusio is a self-contained frame around 43:10-12 that a larger row would have to break through rather than around. The grade rests on these faces: the onset is a turn to the prophet without a counted device, since 43:10's address lacks the conjunction of the counted family, after a samekh on 43:9 that is no signal of its own; the close is the genre colophon in the composition's own voice, and its far face at 43:13 opens the altar's measurements with a list heading, which carries no signal on a far face; the stretch from the glory's return to the torah of the house is one whose division into units is held open, which keeps the row at reduced confidence and no lower.
P10-013.device_notes: Ezek.43.10-Ezek.43.12 itself carries none of the book's 184 parashah occurrences; the samekh at oshb:Ezek.43.9 (single-witness) closes the preceding unit, and the next mark does not fall until the double samekh at 43:27. One K/Q verse disclosed (43:11, doubled note), checked: both disputed forms are possessive-suffix/grammatical-number variants on 'form' and 'law', not numerals. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: one occurrence, at 43:12, the same verse as the doubled inclusio close. Held at 3 verses on the strength of the disclosed sub-onset at 43:10 and the doubled inclusio close at 43:12, not a word-event unit. A separate editors' note is recorded at 43:11 alongside its K/Q pair (single-witness apparatus), disclosed and not argued.

P11-007.boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at Ezek.46.1 opens the Sabbath/new-moon gate rule, itself carrying “the day of the new moon” (web:Ezek.46.1) -- disclosed as a chodesh-root homograph, not a date formula (recurring at 46.6); the construction glossed 'at the new moons' recurs at 46.3, the same homograph family as Ezek.45.17. The unit runs through the prince's Sabbath offering (4-8), the people's festival entry-and-exit rule (9-10), the feast-day meal offering (11-12), and the daily burnt offering (13-15), where Ezek.46.13's 'a lamb of its first year' carries a year word that is explicitly NOT a dateline. The messenger formula at 46:1 is the division set at the head of the chapter, where the law section is divided on its messenger formulae, so the onset is not in question; the reduced confidence rests on the close: 46:15 ends the daily burnt offering with no close-role formula, and the pe recorded after it (single witness) corroborates the paragraph without deciding it. A samekh mark is also recorded after Ezek.46.11 (single witness), mid-unit; it is weighed and disclosed but does not cut, since no messenger-formula or addressee-class change corroborates a seam there -- the next messenger formula is not until 46.16, past the end of this row -- and a parashah mark unaccompanied by a text signal never decides a boundary alone.
P11-007.device_notes: Ezek.46.1 and Ezek.46.6 carry the construction glossed 'the new moon'; Ezek.46.3 carries 'at the new moons' -- all disclosed as the book's chodesh-root homograph family, none a date formula. Ezek.46.13 ('a lamb of its first year') carries a year word explicitly NOT a dateline, disclosed to forestall misreading. The samekh recorded after Ezek.46.11 is single-witness texture, disclosed and non-cutting. The row's close verse, oshb:Ezek.46.15, is a K/Q site: the running text keeps the unpointed ketiv ועשו and the note reads the Qere יַעֲשׂ֨וּ (single-witness apparatus); no boundary is argued from either reading. This row's length, 15 verses, is disclosed as a fact against the 7-10 typical density and is no ground for the grade. Ezek.45.25 is followed by a samekh (single witness), corroborating the onset at Ezek.46.1. Ezek.46.9 is a further K/Q site and Ezek.46.12 carries an editors' note (single-witness apparatus), both disclosed; no boundary is argued from them.

P11-014.boundary_rationale: Onset: no formula device opens Ezek.48.8; the 48.7/48.8 seam behind it rests on the northern block’s own close (the 'one portion' refrain at 48.7) and a change of listed object -- from tribal portions to the holy offering itself. The row covers the dimensions of the holy portion given to the sanctuary, priests and Levites (8-14), the remaining strip for the city and its common land (15-19), the whole square portion set apart with the sanctuary at its centre (20), and the prince's land on either side of the holy portion and the city, framed by Judah's and Benjamin's borders (21-22). A samekh mark is recorded after Ezek.48.11 (single-witness), mid-unit, inside the priests' portion; disclosed, but it does not cut, since it is unaccompanied by any change of addressee or genre and the holy-portion description continues without a fresh onset. Close: the next verse, 48.23, reopens the tribal-portion list on its own resumption formula, a change of listed object back from the holy portion, city and prince to the southern tribes -- a real content seam at the list's internal division, formula-free like this row's own onset.
P11-014.device_notes: Neither this row's onset at 48.8 nor its close before 48.23 carries a formula device; both are argued from a change of listed object, disclosed as such. The samekh recorded after Ezek.48.11 is single-witness, mid-unit, non-cutting. Measured on the witness, neither near face carries a counted signal and the refrain at 48.7 behind the onset is no counted close formula, which holds the row at reduced confidence. Paseq is recorded within Ezek.48.18 (one), Ezek.48.21 (three) and Ezek.48.22 (one), count-only, single-witness; five K/Q sites fall inside the row, at 48:14, 48:15, 48:16, 48:18 and 48:21 (single-witness apparatus), none argued for a boundary.

P01-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.8 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם … (WEB “But you, son of man, hear” (web:Ezek.2.8)) turns to the prophet with a ve'attah address, but the addressee does not change, since 2:7 already speaks to him, and 2:7 ends on the rebellion refrain כִּ֥י מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה (oshb:Ezek.2.7), which is no close-role formula; the ve'attah onset is therefore unlicensed, and the pe recorded after oshb:Ezek.2.7 (single-witness) corroborates the break without licensing it. The scroll appears at 2:9, וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּה יָ֖ד שְׁלוּחָ֣ה אֵלָ֑י וְהִנֵּה (oshb:Ezek.2.9) (“behold, a hand was stretched out to me” (web:Ezek.2.9)), and its inscription is read at 2:10, אֵלֶ֔יהָ קִנִ֥ים וָהֶ֖גֶה וָהִֽי (oshb:Ezek.2.10) ('lamentations, mourning, and woe'); the samekh recorded after 2:10 stands at the 2:10/3:1 seam and is disclosed as texture inside the row rather than a cut, since the eating that follows continues the same scroll scene: 3:1 reopens with a further 'he said to me,' אֱכוֹל֙ אֶת הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את (oshb:Ezek.3.1) ('eat this scroll'), intra-row, and the WEB chapter numeral falling at 2:10/3:1 is disclosed only as texture, never as boundary evidence. Close: 3:3, וַתְּהִ֥י בְּפִ֖י כִּדְבַ֥שׁ לְמָתֽוֹק (oshb:Ezek.3.3) ('it was in my mouth as sweet as honey'), with a pe recorded after it, before the address turns from the scroll to the audience's character at 3:4. That close rests on the report of the eating, which carries no close-role formula, while its far face 3:4 opens on a further 'he said to me' inside the vision; with the onset's ve'attah unlicensed and no close-role formula at the close, neither of the row's own near faces carries a licensed signal, which is why the row carries reduced confidence.
P01-003.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between 2:10 and 3:1, where the WEB prints a chapter break and a samekh is recorded after 2:10 (single-witness). Rejected because 3:1's 'he said to me', a licensed onset inside the vision, continues the same scroll scene the samekh only pauses: it commands the prophet to eat the scroll whose writing 2:10 has just described. Treating the WEB chapter numeral as a boundary would read the translation's layout as if it were evidence in the Hebrew witness.
P01-003.device_notes: Samekh after 2:10 (single-witness) disclosed as intra-row texture: the eating (3:1-3:3) continues under the 'he said to me' at 3:1, so the mark is not read as a unit-cutting seam. A second 'he said to me' heads 3:3, a licensed onset at the 3:2/3:3 seam, weighed and not taken: its far face 3:2 reports the eating itself with no close-role formula, and 3:3 repeats the command to the same prophet and completes the eating that 3:1 began, so a cut would strand a one-verse remainder that is no complete unit. The WEB paragraph/chapter break at 2:10/3:1 is named nowhere as boundary evidence.

P01-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting after 5:13 or after 5:15, the first two 'I Yahweh have spoken' occurrences, to shorten the unit. Rejected because neither is followed by a fresh onset device - the material after each continues the same verdict speech without a messenger formula, word-event or address restarting it - so only 5:17's occurrence is unit-final. The stronger rival, also weighed here, is the 5:4/5:5 seam, where the sign-act command to the prophet ends and the oracle concerning Jerusalem begins, which would set the sign-act 5:1-4 against the interpretation 5:5-17. Its far face carries a PE recorded after oshb:Ezek.5.4 (single witness) and nothing further: that verse ends מִמֶּ֥נּוּ תֵצֵא אֵ֖שׁ אֶל כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and it is neither an utterance-formula verse nor one of the verses of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), so it does not close on a close-role formula. Its near face is genuinely strong, oshb:Ezek.5.5 carrying the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה verse-initially, “The Lord Yahweh says” (web:Ezek.5.5). But a messenger formula counts as a sub-onset only where the addressee changes or the preceding verse has closed on a verse-final close-role formula, and neither condition holds at this seam: 5:4 addresses the prophet in the 2ms while 5:5 carries no second person at all, the shift to 2mp arriving only at 5:7 and to 2fs at 5:8; and a parashah mark cannot meet the second condition by itself. The row accordingly holds the seam on those stated grounds, and the PE is recorded as corroboration of the rival and not of this unit's onset.
P01-009.device_notes: 17-verse unit, the whole chapter, over the 7-10 verse target; disclosed as over the target rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut, as at oshb:Ezek.4.1-4.17, since no refrain-plus-fresh-onset pair stands anywhere inside 5:1-5:17 to license a shorter cut. Paseq at 5:1 and 5:7 disclosed count-only, single-witness. Marks after 5:4 (pe), 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 (samekh) and 5:10 (pe) are disclosed as intra-row, single-witness texture. Three of those five marks coincide with a formula onset on the verse following them. The pe after 5:4 stands before the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.5.5, and the samekh marks after 5:6 and 5:7 stand before the messenger formulae at oshb:Ezek.5.7 and oshb:Ezek.5.8; each of those three verses is one of the 122 verses carrying the long messenger formula, and each carries it verse-initially, 5:7 behind לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Ezek.5.7) and 5:8 behind לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Ezek.5.8). The remaining two do not: oshb:Ezek.5.10 opens on לָכֵ֗ן with no messenger formula, and oshb:Ezek.5.11 opens on the oath with the utterance signature attached mid-verse. No one of the five is read as a unit-cutting seam, and the reason is not any absence of coincidence. A messenger formula is a sub-onset when the addressee changes or when the verse before it ENDS on a close-role formula. The second condition fails at all five, since none of 5:4, 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 or 5:10 carries an utterance formula or belongs to the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), and a parashah mark by itself cannot meet it. The first condition does not cut here either: the second-person plural address at 5:7 and the feminine singular at 5:8 turn to Jerusalem and the people within her, whom the verdict treats as a single party, and 5:10 and 5:11 carry no messenger formula at all. Single witness: a pe stands after MT 4:17, the mark this witness sets at the seam where this unit begins.

P01-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: 7:5 reopens with a fresh messenger formula immediately after 7:4's recognition close, which a pe follows (single-witness) — כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.7.5) “The Lord Yahweh says: ‘A disaster! A unique disaster! Behold, it comes.” (web:Ezek.7.5). Close: 7:9, the 2mp recognition-family close carrying an appended participle, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.7.9) “Then you will know that I, Yahweh, strike.” (web:Ezek.7.9); this recognition member also carries the doubled “My eye will not spare” (web:Ezek.7.4) refrain — MEASURED at 5 verses book-wide (5:11, 7:4, 7:9, 8:18, 9:10) by a consonantal-skeleton sweep of the phrase *lo tachos eini* over the pointed Hebrew witness, the WEB contracting the clause at every one of those verses except 7:4, which is why the quotation cites web:Ezek.7.4 — the same refrain the close at 7:4 already carries, so 7:9 closes a distinct short unit before the unmarked doom-poem reopens at 7:10 with no formula of its own.
P01-013.device_notes: Five-verse unit; justified by the fresh messenger-formula onset at 7:5 and the doubled-refrain recognition close at 7:9 (shared with 7:4), not by size. Disclosed as short, not capped. MEASURED in this witness (single-witness), which records a mark on the verse it follows: a pe is recorded on MT 7:4, so the witness breaks immediately before this row's first verse; inside the row, 7:5-7:8 carry no mark; and at the close no samekh and no pe is recorded on MT 7:9. The witness's own sectioning, read against this row: the next mark after the pe on MT 7:4 is the pe on MT 7:22, so the witness's own open section runs 7:5-7:22 and this row's close at 7:9 falls inside it. That sectioning corroborates the longer rival rather than this row, and it is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates. It does not unseat the row: a section boundary of the witness is weak corroboration that never outranks a licensed text signal, and the near face of this close carries one — the 2mp recognition clause at 7:9, whose only word after the formula is the dependent participle מַכֶּֽה (MEASURED: in the verse's consonantal skeleton, the clause quoted here in pointed form, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה occupies characters 63-80 of 84, counting from 1 with both ends included, with מַכֶּֽה filling the remainder), so it is verse-final in effect and grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal rather than the weak mid-verse shape. The absence of a mark at 7:9 is disclosed and is never read as counter-evidence (oshb:Ezek.7.9).

P02-004.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is a cut between 9:8 and 9:9, where 'he said to me' opens 9:9 inside the vision, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.9.9), a licensed near face. P02-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.12.1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, the strict word-event formula, opens the collection of undated oracles immediately after the vision report closes at 11:25; oshb:Ezek.12.2 names the addressee 'the rebellious house' (בית המרי), the disputation refrain that the commission narrative of chapters 2-3 also uses; the phrase, with or without the article, stands on 12 verses of this witness book-wide (MEASURED), six of them in chapters 2-3. MT 11:25 is followed by a pe (single witness), corroborating the onset of this unit at 12:1. Close: oshb:Ezek.12.7 וָאַ֣עַשׂ כֵּן֮ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צֻוֵּיתִי֒ כֵּ֠לַי הוֹצֵ֜אתִי כִּכְלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וּבָעֶ֛רֶב חָתַֽרְתִּי לִ֥י בַקִּ֖יר בְּיָ֑ד בָּעֲלָטָ֥ה הוֹצֵ֛אתִי עַל כָּתֵ֥ף נָשָׂ֖אתִי לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם — “I did so as I was commanded.” (web:Ezek.12.7) — reports the sign-act's execution, immediately before a fresh word-event at oshb:Ezek.12.8 reopens with an infixed 'in the morning' phrase. A pe follows oshb:Ezek.12.7 (single-witness). The onset seam is two-faced: 11:25 completes the vision's return, and 12:1 carries the strict word-event formula (sweep: 39 verses). The close seam is weaker on its near side: 12:7 reports the sign-act's execution with no close-role formula, the pe after it corroborating without licensing it, while its far face 12:8 carries the word-event formula with a phrase inserted into it (one of the two verses in the 41-verse vayehi-any word-event count whose formula an inserted phrase interrupts, here 'in the morning'). That execution report without a formula is the ground of the lower grade.
P02-011.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 12:1-16 as one sixteen-verse row (the sign-act and its full interpretation together) was weighed, since nothing but the 12:8 re-onset separates the command from the interpretation. It was not taken because 12:8 is itself a genuine word-event onset (its formula carrying the infixed 'in the morning', one of the only two vayehi-any verses the strict adjacent form misses) that turns from the act to its meaning, and a pe (single-witness) stands after the 12:7 stopping point, corroborating the cut without deciding it.

P03-010.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 17:1 opens (oshb:Ezek.17.1) with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, and 17:2 names the genre directly, בֶּן אָדָ֕ם ח֥וּד חִידָ֖ה וּמְשֹׁ֣ל מָשָׁ֑ל אֶל בֵּ֖ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.17.2) (rendered “Son of man, tell a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Israel”, web:Ezek.17.2), before the messenger formula כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.17.3) opens the eagle-and-vine figure itself. Close side: this row runs through 17:10, whose concluding clause תִּיבַ֣שׁ יָבֹ֔שׁ (oshb:Ezek.17.10) ('it will surely wither') answers the riddle's own rhetorical question, matched by a pe recorded on this same verse in the single-witness paragraph layer -- the riddle's content is complete and the mark coincides with it, so the row is closed here before the interpretation opens with its own word-event formula at 17:11. The onset is two-faced, 16:63 ending on the utterance formula verse-finally with a samekh after it against the word-event formula at 17:1. The close is not: its near face, 17:10, ends on the riddle's answer with no close-role formula, a content close the book-wide formula counts do not list, and the pe is corroboration that licenses nothing. That near face, against the word-event formula on the far face at 17:11, is what keeps the row's confidence reduced.
P03-010.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the riddle and its interpretation as one long row (17:1-24) was weighed and not taken: 17:11 opens with its own strict word-event formula, byte-identical to 17:1's, and the pe on 17:10 (single-witness) corroborates a break exactly where the riddle's own question is answered.

P03-014.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:1 opens on the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.18.1); 18:2 quotes the popular proverb the oracle will refute, אָבוֹת֙ יֹ֣אכְלוּ בֹ֔סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה (oshb:Ezek.18.2) (“The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge”, web:Ezek.18.2). Close side: the span closes at 18:4, whose final clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֥יא תָמֽוּת (oshb:Ezek.18.4) ('the soul who sins shall die') states the disputation's thesis, and a samekh stands on this same verse (single-witness). An oath formula with the utterance signature stands at the head of 18:3, in that verse's first five words ('as I live, declares the Lord YHWH'), weighed as texture inside the refutation rather than a row-final close, since the clause on the proverb's future use runs on after it to the end of the same verse. The close at 18:4/18:5 is a case turn inside one word-event unit: 18:4 ends on the disputation's thesis and carries a samekh, 18:5 opens the righteous-man case with no formula of its own, and the samekh corroborates that turn without deciding it. A close seam of that shape holds a row at reduced confidence, and this row is held there. The onset seam, by contrast, is two-faced and top grade: 17:24 ends on the I-YHWH-have-spoken formula, verse-final, with a pe recorded after it (single-witness), against 18:1's strict word-event formula.
P03-014.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 18:9 (thesis plus the first case-law example together) was weighed and not taken: the samekh on 18:4 (single-witness) corroborates a close for the thesis statement alone without deciding it, and 18:5 opens the righteous-man case with no formula of its own -- a fresh case argued on its own terms, rather than an illustration folded into the thesis that precedes it.

P03-021.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is a cut between 18:23 and 18:24, which would set the repentance case apart from the reverse case and the appeal. Its far face, 18:23, carries the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה mid-verse, with the rhetorical question הֲל֛וֹא בְּשׁוּב֥וֹ מִדְּרָכָ֖יו וְחָיָֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.23) running on after it to the verse's end, and a samekh follows the verse (single-witness); its near face, 18:24, opens the case of the righteous man who turns away, with no formula device. A mid-verse formula ends nothing and a mark alone licenses no cut, so the seam is paragraph-grade. The row holds against it because 18:24 states the mirror image of the case 18:21-22 has just stated, and the objection quoted at 18:25 and again at 18:29 is raised against both cases together.
P03-021.device_notes: Ketiv/qere notes stand in this span at 18:21, 18:24 and 18:28, one note on each verse (single-witness apparatus), none quoted here; 18:29 carries the witness's editorial note that BHS keeps the Leningrad Codex form where its validity might be questioned, and that form is kept. No paseq falls inside 18:21-32. Marks (single-witness): a samekh after 18:20 at the onset seam, a samekh after 18:23 and another after 18:26 inside the span, and a pe after 18:32 at the close seam. The cut between 18:26 and 18:27 was weighed and not taken: the only device it could rest on is the samekh after 18:26, and the positive case at 18:27 opens with no formula. The cut between 18:29 and 18:30 was weighed and not taken: the therefore-turn at 18:30 answers the objection quoted at 18:29, carries the utterance formula only mid-verse, and has no mark before it.

P03-021.boundary_rationale: Onset: 18:21 opens the case of the wicked man who turns, וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ (oshb:Ezek.18.21) (“But if the wicked turns from all his sins” (web:Ezek.18.21)), with no onset-class device of its own; its far face 18:20 closes the preceding case on the principle that a person's own righteousness or wickedness rests on that person, and ends on no close-role formula, the samekh after it (single-witness) corroborating the break only. Close: 18:32 carries the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.18.32) mid-verse, and the independent imperative וְהָשִׁ֖יבוּ וִֽחְיֽוּ (oshb:Ezek.18.32) follows it, “Therefore turn yourselves, and live!” (web:Ezek.18.32), so the formula does not stand at the verse's end; a pe follows the verse, and the far face 19:1 opens on the command to take up a lament, וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.19.1). Between these seams the span makes one appeal: the wicked man who turns (18:21-23), the righteous man who turns away (18:24), the people's objection, the two cases restated and the objection repeated (18:25-29), and the closing appeal (18:30-32). The utterance formula standing mid-verse in 18:23 with a samekh after it, the samekh after 18:26, and the therefore-turn at 18:30 mark paragraphs inside that one appeal, and none of them carries a licensed onset. Neither of the row's own near faces carries a licensed signal, since the onset opens with no formula and the close's formula stands mid-verse, and only the far face of the close, 19:1, is licensed; the row is held at reduced confidence on those faces.

P05-004.boundary_rationale: Onset: 23:1, whole verse = "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.23.1)", the strict word-event formula. Close: 23:21, whole verse = "וַֽתִּפְקְדִ֔י אֵ֖ת זִמַּ֣ת נְעוּרָ֑יִךְ בַּעְשׂ֤וֹת מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ דַּדַּ֔יִךְ לְמַ֖עַן שְׁדֵ֥י נְעוּרָֽיִךְ (oshb:Ezek.23.21)", ends on the address to Oholibah with no close-role formula, and a samekh follows it (single-witness). Past the seam 23:22 opens on a therefore-turn with the messenger formula and the vocative אָהֳלִיבָ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.23.22), but the second-person feminine address already stands in 23:21, so the formula turns to the verdict without changing the addressee and licenses no onset of its own. A close whose near face carries no formula and whose far face carries no licensed onset is what holds this row at reduced confidence; the onset, by contrast, is two-faced, the utterance formula ending 22:31 verse-finally against the word-event formula at 23:1. Between 23:1 and 23:21 there is no formula-marked internal seam: the narrative subject shifts from Oholah (23:5-10) to Oholibah (23:11-21) without a word-event, messenger formula, or "and you, son of man" device at the shift point, so the 21-verse span is held as one unit rather than forcing an unsupported cut.
P05-004.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting between 23:10 and 23:11, where Oholah's narrative ends and Oholibah's begins (23:11 opens "וַתֵּ֨רֶא֙ אֲחוֹתָ֣הּ אָהֳלִיבָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.23.11)...") — this has some real support (a samekh mark after 23:10, single-witness, and a clear subject shift) but is REJECTED as a boundary because an internal cut rests on a licensed onset device at the seam: a formula, a transport verb, or a speech introduction inside a vision, and 23:11 carries none of them. This unit runs 21 verses, over the 7-10 verse target, a length disclosed as fact.

P05-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 23:22 opens on a therefore-turn with the messenger formula and the vocative naming Oholibah, whole verse = "לָכֵ֣ן אָהֳלִיבָ֗ה כֹּֽה אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנְנִ֨י מֵעִ֤יר אֶת מְאַהֲבַ֨יִךְ֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר נָקְעָ֥ה נַפְשֵׁ֖ךְ מֵהֶ֑ם וַהֲבֵאתִ֥ים עָלַ֖יִךְ מִסָּבִֽיב (oshb:Ezek.23.22)". The second-person feminine singular address does not begin here: it already stands in 23:21, which opens וַֽתִּפְקְדִ֔י (oshb:Ezek.23.21), 'and you called to mind', with second-person feminine suffixes through the verse, so the vocative names the sister already addressed and the formula turns from indictment to verdict without an addressee change. 23:21 ends with no close-role formula, and the samekh after it (single witness) corroborates the turn without licensing it. The book's division names a cut at 23:22 on the premise of a messenger formula with an addressee change, a premise these bytes do not bear; the seam is kept as that named cut and held as a paragraph-grade seam. Close: 23:35, whole verse = "לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֚עַן שָׁכַ֣חַתְּ אוֹתִ֔י וַתַּשְׁלִ֥יכִי אוֹתִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֣י גַוֵּ֑ךְ וְגַם אַ֛תְּ שְׂאִ֥י זִמָּתֵ֖ךְ וְאֶת תַּזְנוּתָֽיִךְ (oshb:Ezek.23.35)" — a "therefore... because" verdict-summary still addressed to Oholibah and ending on no close-role formula, immediately before 23:36, where 'YHWH said to me' and the 'son of man' address turn the speech from Oholibah to the prophet, who is asked to judge both sisters (weighed as the following unit's onset). CLOSE-SEAM MARK: MEASURED in this witness, MT 23:35 is followed by a SAMEKH (setumah, closed section, single-witness). Because a mark is recorded on the verse it follows, this one stands on THIS row's close seam at 23:35/23:36 - not behind the onset and not mid-unit - so the close is corroborated by the mark and licensed on its far face by the change of addressee at 23:36. A licensed text signal outranks a section mark, so the samekh is weak corroboration and decides nothing alone. One further measured fact is stated here without being acted on, because it bears on the rejected alternative rather than on this disclosure: MT 23:34 ends verse-finally on the utterance formula (oshb:Ezek.23.34), which means the messenger formula opening MT 23:35 stands right after a verse that ends on a close-role formula, and that alone licenses it as a sub-onset, so the 23:34/23:35 rival is a licensed, two-faced rival and not one defeated by addressee continuity alone. The close stays at 23:35, and the question of that seam remains open. Holding that rival on stated grounds does not decide this row's confidence, which rests on its own near faces: the onset formula at 23:22 changes no addressee and follows no close-role formula, and the close at 23:35 ends on no close-role formula, so the row is held at reduced confidence.
P05-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing this unit at 23:34 instead of 23:35 — 23:34 carries the stronger formula-close evidence (the utterance formula verse-final, plus a samekh after it, single-witness), whole verse = "וְשָׁתִ֨ית אוֹתָ֜הּ וּמָצִ֗ית וְאֶת חֲרָשֶׂ֛יהָ תְּגָרֵ֖מִי וְשָׁדַ֣יִךְ תְּנַתֵּ֑קִי כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י דִבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.23.34)". P05-006.boundary_rationale: Onset: 23:36 is a sub-onset — "YHWH said to me" plus the "son of man" address, which turns the address from Oholibah, spoken to in the second person singular through 23:35, to the prophet, who is asked to judge BOTH sisters — whole verse = "וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הֲתִשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶֽת אָהֳלָ֖ה וְאֶת אָהֳלִיבָ֑ה וְהַגֵּ֣ד לָהֶ֔ן אֵ֖ת תוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶֽן (oshb:Ezek.23.36)". The seam's far face, 23:35, ends on a verdict clause with no close-role formula; the messenger formula at its head is a sub-onset inside the unit that ends at 23:35, not a signal on this seam, and the seam's strength here is the addressee change at 23:36. This is not a hard seam (the hard seams inside this collection are the dateline and word-event onsets at 22:1, 22:17, 22:23, 23:1, 24:1 and 24:15; 23:36 is not among them); it is instead a held either/or question — its own unit, or the close of the 23:1-35 allegory — rather than a hard seam. Close: 23:49, whole verse = "וְנָתְנ֤וּ זִמַּתְכֶ֨נָה֙ עֲלֵיכֶ֔ן וַחֲטָאֵ֥י גִלּוּלֵיכֶ֖ן תִּשֶּׂ֑אינָה וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.23.49)" — ending in a recognition-formula-pattern clause (2mp verb form with the "Lord YHWH" divine-name variant, read directly from these bytes rather than from any pre-counted inventory list), followed by a pe mark (single-witness).
P05-006.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 23:36-49 as the CLOSE of the single 23:1-49 allegory rather than its own unit — this is a live alternative and it is not dismissed here, only not taken: 23:36's combination of a fresh address formula and an addressee change is read as closer in kind to a fresh unit-opening than to a coda, so it is written as its own unit, held at medium confidence rather than high.

P06-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:11 opens with the strict word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.28.11). 28:12 supplies the genre command, "בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שָׂ֥א קִינָ֖ה עַל מֶ֣לֶךְ צ֑וֹר וְאָמַ֣רְתָּ לּ֗וֹ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה אַתָּה֙ חוֹתֵ֣ם תָּכְנִ֔ית מָלֵ֥א חָכְמָ֖ה וּכְלִ֥יל יֹֽפִי" — “Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre” (web:Ezek.28.12, WEB) — the same imperative-plus-קִינָ֖ה anchor as 27:2, naming the addressee "king" (מֶ֣לֶךְ (oshb:Ezek.28.12)) rather than 28:2's "prince" (לִנְגִ֨יד (oshb:Ezek.28.2)). In the WEB, “Son of man, take up a lamentation over the king of Tyre, and tell him, ‘The Lord Yahweh says:” (web:Ezek.28.12). Close: 28:19 ends "כָּל יוֹדְעֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּֽעַמִּ֔ים שָׁמְמ֖וּ עָלֶ֑יךָ בַּלָּה֣וֹת הָיִ֔יתָ וְאֵינְךָ֖ עַד עוֹלָֽם" (oshb:Ezek.28.19) with a PE immediately after (single-witness) and no recognition/utterance/"I YHWH have spoken" formula present; the close pattern “You have become a terror, and you will exist no more.” (web:Ezek.28.19, WEB) mirrors MT 27:36's terminal clause in the CONSONANTAL Hebrew and not in the translation - MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, the two verses end consonant for consonant on the same six words and differ there only in the Masoretic pointing, feminine singular at MT 27:36 against masculine singular at MT 28:19, while the WEB renders MT 27:36 quite differently as “You have come to a terrible end, and you will be no more.” (web:Ezek.27.36, WEB); the exact mirror holds of the Hebrew consonants alone. Behind, 28:10 closed the prince-of-Tyre unit on the stacked "I have spoken" + utterance close and a SAMEKH, against 28:11's strict word-event, so the onset seam is two-faced; ahead, 28:20 opens a fresh strict word-event onset for the Sidon oracle. The close's near face is the weak one: the shared terminal line of 28:19 is a refrain that the counted formula classes do not include, a close without formula, and that near face is what the lower grade rests on.

P07-008.boundary_rationale: Onset side: the hard-seam dateline at oshb:Ezek.32.17 (year 12, day 15, with no month named in the verse -- 32:1 carries the twelfth month and this dateline carries none; perfect hayah word-event form) opens onto the son-of-man command at oshb:Ezek.32.18 to “wail for the multitude of Egypt” (web:Ezek.32.18) -- a different technical verb from the qinah noun that opened and closed 32:1-16, disclosed as a genre question rather than assumed continuous with it. Close side: the row runs through the taunt (32:19-21) and the protected, never-cut roster of fallen nations in Sheol (32:22-30) to the doubled utterance-formula close at oshb:Ezek.32.31 and oshb:Ezek.32.32, corroborated by a following pe (single-witness), where the collection of oracles against the nations closes. The genre call (oracle_against_nation vs. lament_qinah) is held, not resolved; it does not bear on the seam grade. Both seams are two-faced and top grade: 32:16 ends on the utterance signature, verse-final, and carries a pe, against 32:17's dateline and hayah-form word-event; and 32:32 ends on the utterance signature, verse-final, with a pe after it, against the strict word-event formula at 33:1. Inside the span 32:31 ends on the utterance formula while 32:32 opens on כִּֽי (oshb:Ezek.32.32) with no onset-class device, so that recurrence is paragraph-grade and not a rival; 32:18's son-of-man address corroborates the onset rather than opening a unit of its own; and the roster at 32:22-30 is never cut. No licensed or two-faced rival stands anywhere in the span, and its 16 verses are the whole Sheol oracle built around that roster, so the length is no ground against it. That is what this row's high grade records.

MT 32:16 carries a following pe, single witness, at this unit's own onset seam. onset bytes (oshb:Ezek.32.17): וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר | close bytes (oshb:Ezek.32.32): כִּֽי נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת חתיתו בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַיִּ֑ים וְהֻשְׁכַּב֩ בְּת֨וֹךְ עֲרֵלִ֜ים אֶת חַלְלֵי חֶ֗רֶב פַּרְעֹה֙ וְכָל הֲמוֹנֹ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה

P08-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: MT 33:20 is followed by a pe (single-witness), corroborating the onset at 33:21; that pe stands where this witness records no sof pasuq on MT 33:20, and it is the only corroboration the onset carries from behind. The dateline at Ezek.33.21 וַיְהִ֞י בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לְגָלוּתֵ֑נוּ בָּא אֵלַ֨י הַפָּלִ֧יט מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר הֻכְּתָ֥ה הָעִֽיר (oshb:Ezek.33.21) — one of the book's 14 year-bearing oracle datelines and a hard seam — reports the fugitive's arrival with news the city has fallen. Ezek.33.22 וְיַד יְהוָה֩ הָיְתָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בָּעֶ֗רֶב לִפְנֵי֙ בּ֣וֹא הַפָּלִ֔יט וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח אֶת פִּ֔י עַד בּ֥וֹא אֵלַ֖י בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיִּפָּ֣תַח פִּ֔י וְלֹ֥א נֶאֱלַ֖מְתִּי עֽוֹד (oshb:Ezek.33.22) follows with the hand-of-YHWH idiom (matched on the construct alone, one of 7 verses carrying the construct) and the mouth-opening event that fulfils the muteness first commissioned in ch. 3 and anticipated as a coming sign earlier in the book. This hand-of-YHWH occurrence opens no vision here — it is narrative notice, not a scene-transport marker. Close: a pe mark follows Ezek.33.22 (single-witness), and the verse completes the narrative beat before Ezek.33.23 opens a fresh, formally distinct word-event oracle. The onset's near face is licensed -- the dateline itself -- while the far face behind it carries that mark and no formula. The close's near face, 33:22, carries no close-role signal: its hand-of-YHWH idiom is narrative notice, and the verse ends on the mouth-opening clause with no formula, while its far face is 33:23's fresh word-event formula. That close near face is the ground of this row's reduced confidence.
P08-003.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding these two verses into the head of Ezek.33.23-Ezek.33.29, on the model of shared-word-event spans elsewhere (e.g. Ezek.35.1/Ezek.36.1). Rejected because 33.23 opens its OWN fresh word-event formula rather than continuing 33.21's dateline frame — unlike the 35.1/36.1 pairing, there is no shared onset device to disclose across a merged row, so folding them would combine two formally distinct onset types into one row rather than extend one shared frame. Held instead as its own 2-verse unit: 33:21 opens on its dateline, and 33:22's hand-of-YHWH narrative notice together with the pe that follows it (single-witness) close the unit before 33:23's own fresh word-event formula opens the next.
P08-003.device_notes: The category is a disclosed deviation read from the bytes: the row is classed as a commission narrative (the muteness/mouth-opening device) rather than a vision report, because the hand-of-YHWH here is followed by narrative notice (the mouth-opening at Ezek.33.22) rather than any scene-transport or vision-inaugurating formula, and rather than a disputation or judgment oracle because the verses are narrative notice, not oracle speech. Under-3-verse row, disclosed as a two-verse unit bounded by 33:21's own dateline onset and the pe after 33:22 (single-witness).

P08-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: the sub-onset “As for you, son of man,” (web:Ezek.33.30) at Ezek.33.30 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם בְּנֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֗ הַנִּדְבָּרִ֤ים בְּךָ֙ אֵ֣צֶל הַקִּיר֔וֹת וּבְפִתְחֵ֖י הַבָּתִּ֑ים וְדִבֶּר חַ֣ד אֶת אַחַ֗ד אִ֤ישׁ אֶת אָחִיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֹּֽאוּ נָ֣א וְשִׁמְע֔וּ מָ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר הַיּוֹצֵ֖א מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.33.30) opens a new complaint about the people's reception of the prophet, distinct from the land-inheritance dispute just closed. Close: the chapter's final verse, Ezek.33.33 וּבְבֹאָ֑הּ הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֔ה וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י נָבִ֖יא הָיָ֥ה בְתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.33.33), states the outcome (“then they will know that a prophet has been among them” (web:Ezek.33.33)) in a clause that functions like a recognition close but does not match the standard 'know that I am Yahweh' formula bytes; it is disclosed here as a non-formulaic close rather than claimed as formula-count membership. A samekh mark follows Ezek.33.33 (single-witness), corroborating the chapter's own end, immediately before Ezek.34.1's fresh word-event (hard seam). The onset is licensed on both faces: 33:29 ends on the recognition formula with only a dependent clause after it, and the 'and you, son of man' address at 33:30 follows that close. The close is not: its near face carries only a recognition-shaped clause that the book-wide count of recognition formulae does not include, so it offers no licensed signal, while its far face, 34:1, carries the strict word-event formula; that near face holds the row at reduced confidence.
P08-005.device_notes: The disputation-oracle category fits 33.30-33 as one unit, with no departure from it. Close is explicitly flagged as non-formulaic so as not to inflate any of the book's recognition-formula counts.
