P09-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: a messenger formula reopens at oshb:Ezek.39.25 לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה עַתָּ֗ה אָשִׁיב֙ אֶת שבית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֖י כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְקִנֵּאתִ֖י לְשֵׁ֥ם קָדְשִֽׁי on the word ‘therefore,’ immediately turning from the exile retrospective to the restoration promise. That turn addresses the same hearers as the retrospective before it, so it is a discourse turn and not a licensed sub-onset, and the far face behind it, oshb:Ezek.39.24, carries a samekh (single-witness) and no close-role formula -- its hidden-face clause is not a close device -- so the onset seam is corroborated by a mark alone. In 39.25 the ketiv reads שבית (oshb:Ezek.39.25, ketiv) and the qere reads שְׁב֣וּת (oshb:Ezek.39.25, Qere) (a single-witness textual-variant site, disclosed, never argued as a boundary). Close: 39.25-29 ends at oshb:Ezek.39.29 וְלֹֽא אַסְתִּ֥יר ע֛וֹד פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁפַ֤כְתִּי אֶת רוּחִי֙ עַל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה, the standard utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature (one of 81 book-wide) with a pe mark recorded immediately after -- the close evidence the restoration collection's own boundary is anchored on, matching the point where the following material opens on a dateline plus hand-of-YHWH and transport at Ezek.40.1. The close seam stands top grade on both faces -- 39.29's utterance signature with the pe recorded after it, and the dateline with hand-of-YHWH and transport at 40.1 past it -- while the onset seam's near face is a therefore-turn messenger formula that neither a change of addressee nor a verse-final close licenses, and that unlicensed near face is what grounds this row's reduced confidence.
P09-011.device_notes: No paseq falls in this span. MT 39:25 is a single-note K/Q verse (written שבית (oshb:Ezek.39.25, ketiv), read שְׁב֣וּת (oshb:Ezek.39.25, Qere)); no editorial note falls here. The span closes at 39:29, the restoration collection's own close; no material past 39:29 is claimed. The strict recognition formula stands at 39:28, interior to the span and not its close. The hidden-face clause that ends 39:24 recurs, negated, at 39:29, straddling this row's onset seam; it argues continuity across the seam and is disclosed as such.

P10-004.device_notes: No parashah mark touches ch 40 at all. Four of the book's twenty-three doubled-note K/Q verses fall inside this row (40:21, 40:22, 40:24, 40:26), plus a single note at 40:25; every one checked here is the recurring defective/plene 3ms possessive-suffix pattern on architectural nouns (chambers, posts, porches, windows, palm-trees), never on the cubit figures. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: one occurrence, at 40:25; the position of the stroke within the verse is not stated; it is counted by verse. The transport at 40:24, weighed as a rival seam in the rejected alternative, is held inside the row because the book's division keeps the outer north and south gates together as one row and the transport stays inside the outer court.

P10-012.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:1, a verse of the counted transport class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), opens with וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל הַשָּׁ֑עַר (oshb:Ezek.43.1) 'he led me to the gate', at the seam the book's division names as a hard seam, behind the closed measuring circuit, and the row immediately carries the glory-of-YHWH device twice (43:4, 43:5), part of the book's nine-verse departure/return arc for that idiom, alongside the river-Chebar inclusio at 43:3 (one of eight such verses tying this scene back to Ezek 1 and 10) and the prostration “and I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.43.3), one of five verses where the WEB reads “I fell on my face” (sweep: 5 verses). The row turns from vision report to direct address at 43:6-9: a voice from the house, the man beside the prophet, the 'son of man' charge naming YHWH's throne and footstool, and the polemic against the house of Israel's defilement of the sanctuary by royal corpses and high places. Close side: 43:9 ends the divine resolution וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם (oshb:Ezek.43.9) “Then I will dwell among them forever” (web:Ezek.43.9) immediately before the samekh (oshb:Ezek.43.9, single-witness) -- the first Masoretic paragraph mark since the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29, ending a 103-verse unmarked stretch. This close is the first since the pe at 39:29 to carry a parashah mark, and it is disclosed as single-witness even so. Its near face carries no close-role formula: 43:9 ends on the divine resolution, which answers אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֶשְׁכָּן שָׁ֛ם בְּת֥וֹךְ בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעוֹלָ֑ם (oshb:Ezek.43.7) as an inclusio, and past the seam 43:10 opens 'you, son of man' to the same hearer after a verse that ends on no close-role formula, so the seam stands because the book's division names 43:1-9 as the vision and 43:10-12 as the torah of the house. A close of that kind holds this row at reduced confidence, though the onset's near face, the transport verse at 43:1, is licensed.
P10-012.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest rival is a cut between 43:6 and 43:7, a viable tiling of six verses and three. Its near face, 43:7, opens on 'he said to me' inside the vision, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.43.7), a licensed onset; its far face, 43:6, reports “I heard one speaking to me out of the house” (web:Ezek.43.6) and the man standing beside the prophet, and ends on no close-role formula. The cut was not taken: 43:6 announces the speaker whose words 43:7 then gives, so the verse that introduces the voice and the speech it introduces stand together, and the throne declaration at 43:7 is the content the glory's return was staged to deliver.
P10-012.device_notes: The samekh at 43:9 is single-witness Masoretic paragraph evidence, disclosed and treated as corroboration only, never as the sole ground for the seam (the hard-seam onset at 43:1 and the resolution clause at 43:9 stand independently of it). No K/Q or editorial note touches 43:1-43:9. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: one occurrence, at 43:8, inside the defilement polemic. Content note: vv 7-9 carry temple-law-adjacent polemic (royal defilement) inside a row classed as a vision report because the glory-return frame and the throne-declaration speech dominate it. The transport at 43:5, “The Spirit took me up and brought me into the inner court” (web:Ezek.43.5), was weighed as a rival cut between 43:4 and 43:5, a viable tiling of four verses and five, and not taken: its far face, 43:4, ends on the glory entering the house by the east gate with no close-role formula, and the transport carries the prophet in to see that same glory fill the house, so the arrival and its sight are one scene.

P11-006.boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.45.18, following the samekh recorded after Ezek.45.17 (single-witness), opens this row; the law paragraph before it (45.9-17) ends at that samekh on the prince's offerings with no close-role formula, and the hearers do not change, so the formula is not a licensed sub-onset. The samekh corroborates the break, and the seam is kept as a paragraph-grade seam because the book's division of the temple law sets the festival calendar apart as its own law paragraph. Ezek.45.18 also carries a full month+day date construction in the same verse, but the date clause carries no year word, so it fails the book's structural dateline test (a YEAR word together with a month or day term) and is disclosed as NOT a dateline and NOT onset evidence in its own right; it is one of exactly four calendar dates in the book (45.18, 45.20, 45.21, 45.25) that carry a month/day construction without a year, and none of the book's fourteen year-bearing datelines falls anywhere across 44.1-48.35. The unit that follows is the single festival-calendar paragraph running 45.18-25: New Year sanctuary cleansing (18-20, itself containing the non-dateline calendar date at 45.20), Passover (21-24, containing the non-dateline calendar date at 45.21), and the seventh-month feast (25, containing the non-dateline calendar date at 45.25). Close: the samekh recorded after Ezek.45.25 closes both the calendar-law paragraph and the chapter.

P11-008.boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at Ezek.46.16 opens a fresh legal topic -- the prince's inheritance rules -- directly after the pe recorded after Ezek.46.15 (single-witness), on a distinct subject (inheritance, not the cultic calendar) from the cultic-calendar law before it (46.1-15). A change of topic licenses nothing: the hearers do not change, and 46:15 ends on the daily burnt offering with no close-role formula, so the formula is not a licensed sub-onset; the open-section mark corroborates the break, and the seam is paragraph-grade, kept because the book's division sets the prince's inheritance law apart as its own paragraph within the chapter. The row's reduced confidence rests on that onset. The row covers the prince's gift to a son (16), to a servant (17, carrying 'the year of liberty', a year word that is NOT a dateline), and the prohibition on seizing the people's inheritance (18). Close: no parashah mark is recorded on 46.16, 46.17 or 46.18. This row's close is argued instead from the adjacent hard seam at 46.18/46.19, where a transport verb reopens a vision scene -- a shift from temple law to vision report -- a text-signalled close, the samekh recorded after Ezek.46.19 standing beyond the row. The close holds although the row's own last verse carries no parashah mark.
P11-008.device_notes: Ezek.46.17 carries 'the year of liberty', a year word explicitly NOT a dateline, disclosed. This row's close at 46.18/46.19 is a hard seam (a shift from temple law to vision report) rather than a parashah-marked close; the samekh recorded after Ezek.46.19 (single witness) is disclosed at that verse, not here.

P01-008.boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) (“You also, son of man, take a tile” (web:Ezek.4.1)), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that stands at the head of the collection this row opens (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam at oshb:Ezek.3.27. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) (“Behold, I put ropes on you” (web:Ezek.4.8)) repeats the consonantal noun of 3:25 across the parent seam, the two tokens differing in accent; the repetition is recorded here as continuity and carries no seam signal of its own. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act (“behold, I will break the staff of bread” (web:Ezek.4.16)). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) (“that they may lack bread and water” (web:Ezek.4.17)), with a pe following it (single-witness), before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.
P01-008.device_notes: Whole-chapter span disclosed: the unit runs 17 verses, over the 7-10 verse target, and is kept whole rather than forced into an unsupported cut, since no formula-marked seam stands between 4:3/4:4 or 4:8/4:9. Two K/Q verses checked before quoting (4:6, 4:15); 4:6 also carries an editorial note tied to the same disputed consonant, disclosed together. Paseq at 4:9 disclosed count-only, single-witness. MT 3:27 is followed by a samekh (single-witness); the sign-act series that opens at 4:1 has this mark standing immediately before it. Inside the span a samekh follows MT 4:12 (single-witness); the unit does not cut there because the food-rationing act begun at 4:9 continues without a fresh 'son of man' address or messenger formula reopening the speech. A further samekh stands after MT 4:14 (single-witness) inside the span; no cut is made there either, since 4:15's concession is Yahweh's reply within the same rationing scene, not a fresh address. A samekh also follows MT 4:15 (single-witness), inside the span as well; no cut is made there, because the address at 4:16 intensifies the rationing act rather than restarting it.

P02-006.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 10:9-17 as texture inside a larger 10:1-22 (or 10:1-11:13) row rather than its own row was the live alternative and is why this row's confidence rests on the reading alone: no counted formula stands at 10:9, and the wheel material could just as defensibly be folded into the adjacent units at Ezek.10.1-10.8 or Ezek.10.18-10.22. It is kept as its own row because it is a continuous descriptive block, verifiable in the witness bytes at both edges (the wheel vocabulary אוֹפַ֣ן (oshb:Ezek.10.9) and הַגַּלְגַּ֖ל (oshb:Ezek.10.13) clusters in 10:6-17 and 1:15-21 without being confined to them: the wheel noun also stands at 3:13, 10:19 and 11:22, and the companion term at 10:2, 23:24 and 26:10), bounded by narrated action on both sides.

P02-009.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.14 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, the strict word-event formula (one of the book's 39 strict-form onsets), opens an oracle addressed to the exiles rather than to the courtyard men of Ezek.11.1-11.13 — an addressee-class shift inside the vision, from the Jerusalem claimants (oshb:Ezek.11.15, which the WEB renders “This land has been given to us for a possession.” (web:Ezek.11.15)) to “your brothers… the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.11.15) in exile. The witness records a pe after MT 11:13 (single-witness), at the seam this unit opens on at 11:14. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.21 וְאֶל לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה (one of the book's 81 utterance-close verses). The close seam is two-faced: the utterance signature ends 11:21 and the vision's return to the prophet opens at 11:22. The onset's far face is not: MT 11:13 ends on the prophet's own cry and carries no close-role formula, and the pe recorded after it corroborates the paragraph without supplying one. That one bare far face is the evidence this row's confidence reports. This embedded salvation oracle stands inside the still-open vision (the courtyard scene has not yet returned the prophet — that happens only at 11:22-25) but is bounded by its own onset and close formulae independent of the vision frame, so it is set as its own row rather than folded into 11:1-13 or 11:22-25.
P02-009.strongest_rejected_alternative: Holding 11:14-21 inside a single long 11:1-21 courtyard-and-oracle row, with the word-event at 11:14 disclosed only as internal texture, was weighed as an alternative reading. It was not taken because 11:14 is a strict word-event onset (not a bare transition) and the oracle's own addressee — the scattered exiles — differs from the courtyard men addressed in 11:1-13, which is enough of a class shift to justify treating it as its own formula-bounded row even while the wider vision frame stays open around it. A second rival sits inside this row and is weighed here as well: a seam at 11:16/11:17, and behind it a seam at 11:15/11:16. This witness records a samekh after MT 11:15 and another after MT 11:16 (single-witness), and because the witness enters each mark on the verse it stands after, both fall immediately before a verse that carries the long messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה — oshb:Ezek.11.16 and oshb:Ezek.11.17, two of that formula's 122 verses. Neither seam is licensed as a sub-onset, since a messenger formula opens one only if the people addressed change or the verse just before it finishes on a close-role formula. The addressee holds steady: the son-of-man address and the scattered exiles are named at 11:15 and nothing readdresses the oracle before 11:21. Nor does either preceding verse finish on a close-role formula — MEASURED on the pointed witness, MT 11:15 finishes לָ֥נוּ הִ֛יא נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה (oshb:Ezek.11.15) and MT 11:16 finishes בָּאֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.11.16), while in 11:16 and in 11:17 alike the messenger formula stands at the verse's head after לכן אמר rather than at its end. A mark alone cannot stand in for that verse-final formula, so the two samekhs are disclosed for the paragraph structure they corroborate within the row, and the row rests on its strict word-event onset at 11:14 and its verse-final utterance close at 11:21 (MEASURED: נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה closes MT 11:21; oshb:Ezek.11.21).
P02-009.device_notes: Filed under the salvation-oracle category on the restoration promise that is the unit's burden (gather-and-return is stated here: MEASURED at oshb:Ezek.11.17, the oracle both gathers and gives the land — the consonantal skeleton carries וקבצתי אתכם מן העמים ואספתי אתכם מן הארצות and ונתתי לכם את אדמת ישראל, which the WEB renders “I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you out of the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.” (web:Ezek.11.17) — and the “one heart… heart of flesh” (web:Ezek.11.19) promise stands alongside it, so that filing rests on the device the unit actually carries); a one-sentence deviation is disclosed because the unit also carries a disputation-oracle color (the quoted Jerusalem claim at 11:15 is refuted before the promise is given), and the category is not read as free text beyond that single disclosure. No K/Q or paseq falls in this span, on the single-witness apparatus.

P02-018.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.13.17 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל בְּנ֣וֹת עַמְּךָ֔ הַמִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וֹת מִֽלִּבְּהֶ֑ן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽן — “set your face against the daughters of your people” (web:Ezek.13.17) — is one of the book's 9 set-your-face verses and marks an addressee-class shift from the male prophets of 13:1-16, the unit the word-event at oshb:Ezek.13.1 opens, to women “who prophesy out of their own heart” (web:Ezek.13.17). Close: oshb:Ezek.13.23 לָכֵ֗ן שָׁ֚וְא לֹ֣א תֶחֱזֶ֔ינָה וְקֶ֖סֶם לֹא תִקְסַ֣מְנָה ע֑וֹד וְהִצַּלְתִּ֤י אֶת עַמִּי֙ מִיֶּדְכֶ֔ן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ן כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה ends “Then you will know that I am Yahweh.” (web:Ezek.13.23) in the second-feminine-plural form (וידעתן), a counted form of its own (sweep: 2 verses) that belongs to neither the 3mp-28 nor the 2mp-21 recognition class, though both of its verses are members of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), whose members are refrain-grade close evidence; a matching 2fp clause also closes the magic-bands sub-paragraph at oshb:Ezek.13.21. Both sides: the onset's near face carries the counted set-your-face command with its address-class shift, and its far face ends on the verse-final utterance signature of oshb:Ezek.13.16, with a pe following that verse (single-witness); the close's near face ends on the counted feminine-plural recognition form at 13:23, still refrain-grade through the wide family and in the two-verse 2fp form rather than the strict or 2mp class, and its far face opens a fresh scene at web:Ezek.14.1 - “Then some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.” (web:Ezek.14.1) - a scene change read off the narrative rather than off any counted formula class. The interior seam at 13:21 is weighed below and opens on no fresh onset. Both seams therefore stand two-faced with no licensed rival against them, and that is what this row's confidence records.
P02-018.device_notes: The two 2fp recognition clauses at 13:21 and 13:23 are a counted form of their own (sweep: 2 verses), and these two verses are its whole membership; the form is kept apart from the strict recognition class (sweep: 28 verses) and the 2mp family (sweep: 21 verses) and is not added to either; both verses are nonetheless members of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses). Paseq at 13:18 (2x) and 13:20 (1x) is count-only, single-witness. The onset verse also carries the son-of-man address, and a messenger formula stands at 13:18 as well as at 13:20; neither is argued.

P02-020.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.14.12 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, a strict word-event formula, opens the Noah-Daniel-Job oracle on personal versus vicarious righteousness. The unit is a sustained four-scourge refrain list (sword, famine, evil beasts, pestilence, each introduced 'or if…') and is never cut inside it, because a refrain-marked list of this kind is read as one unit across its members; the triad refrain itself recurs, closing each scourge, with the utterance formula co-occurring at oshb:Ezek.14.14, 14.16, 14.18 and 14.20. Onset corroboration: a pe stands after MT 14:11 in this witness (single-witness), at the seam this unit opens on. Close: oshb:Ezek.14.23 וְנִחֲמ֣וּ אֶתְכֶ֔ם כִּֽי תִרְא֥וּ אֶת דַּרְכָּ֖ם וְאֶת עֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֗ם כִּי֩ לֹ֨א חִנָּ֤ם עָשִׂ֨יתִי֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂ֣יתִי בָ֔הּ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה closes this unit with the utterance formula a fifth time, immediately before oshb:Ezek.15.1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר opens the vine mashal with its own fresh strict word-event. A pe follows oshb:Ezek.14.23 (single-witness). Both sides are formula-clean and this closes the unit.
P02-020.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at oshb:Ezek.14.20, where a pe falls after the fourth triad refrain (single-witness) and immediately before the oracle turns from the hypothetical four scourges to their explicit application to Jerusalem (14:21-23), is the standing rival, and it is weighed here rather than passed over. MT 14:21 opens with a messenger formula: MEASURED on this witness's consonantal skeleton, oshb:Ezek.14.21 begins כי כה אמר אדני יהוה, and that verse is among the 122 verses that carry the long messenger formula. What it opens is nonetheless a paragraph, not a sub-onset, since a messenger sub-onset is granted only where the addressee changes or where the verse just before it ENDS on a close-role formula, and neither condition is met. Nothing marks a new addressee at 14:21 — MEASURED, the son-of-man address falls at MT 14:3 and MT 14:13 and at no other verse of this chapter, chapter 14 carries no set-your-face verse at all, and 14:21 is not opened by 'and you, son of man' — so what turns there is the subject, from a hypothetical land to Jerusalem, and not the person addressed. As for the second condition, the utterance formula in MT 14:20 does NOT reach the verse end: MEASURED, נאם אדני יהוה sits at characters 29 through 41 of an 81-character skeleton, the first character counted as 1 and both ends included, and from there the oath's own content runs to the etnachta, with אם בן אם בת יצילו המה בצדקתם יצילו נפשם standing between that signature and the sof pasuq, its second clause independent after the major disjunctive. So the pe on MT 14:20 is entered as support for the rival it favours and for no more than that: this witness records the break after MT 14:20, a mark cannot supply the verse-final close-role formula that the second condition asks for, and paragraph evidence informs while every licensed driver outranks it. The row carries on to its own verse-final utterance close at oshb:Ezek.14.23.
P02-020.device_notes: MT 14:14 and MT 14:20 both carry the Qere-adaptation editorial note class disclosed above, in addition to the ordinary ketiv/qere note at each verse (ketiv דנאל, qere דָּנִיֵּ֣אל (oshb:Ezek.14.14 and oshb:Ezek.14.20) — the shorter legendary-figure spelling against the fuller ‘Daniel’ reading); both disclosures are given at both verses since they are two independent single-witness apparatus facts about the same word. Paseq at 14:21 is count-only, single-witness. oshb:Ezek.15.1 is cited above only as forward-side onset evidence for the seam; it is not a row here. Length disclosure: this row is 12 verses (MEASURED: web:Ezek.14.12-Ezek.14.23, tallied on the WEB face) against a 7-10 verse target length. The over-length is disclosed and carried rather than hidden: the four-scourge refrain list is never cut inside itself, and the one internal seam a reader might take, the messenger paragraph at 14:21, is weighed and held in the rejected alternative.

The onset's near face carries no formula device at all, a turn in the account read rather than counted, and its far face at 16:14 ends verse-final on the utterance formula; the close rests on 16:19's verse-final formula alone, with no parashah mark anywhere in this five-verse stretch (sweep: 5 verses) to corroborate it, single-witness. P03-022.boundary_rationale: Onset: 16:44 opens on the sisters' proverb of mother and daughter, הִנֵּה֙ כָּל הַמֹּשֵׁ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.16.44), and that verse carries no counted onset device - no word-event, messenger formula, son-of-man address, set-your-face command, hand-of-YHWH clause, transport verb or dateline stands in it; the plan names the cut here on content, and a naming that rests on no device licenses nothing. Its far face, MT 16:43, ends the preceding speech, but its utterance formula נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.43) stands mid-verse, with the lewdness clause running past it to the sof pasuq, so no verse-final close-role formula sits behind this onset either. Close: 16:58 ends verse-final on the short utterance נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.58), with a samekh recorded after that verse (single-witness), and its far face at 16:59 opens on the long messenger formula כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.59), which the verse-final close licenses. So the close stands two-faced while the onset's near face carries no licensed signal, and that unlicensed near face, at a seam the plan names on content, is the ground of this row's confidence. Two interior seams are weighed and held, both paragraph-grade: at 16:50/16:51 the comparison turns to Samaria after the samekh recorded on 16:50 (single-witness) and meets a verse with no onset device, and at 16:52/16:53 the restoration turn opens with no device of its own. The span runs fifteen verses against a 7-10 verse target, disclosed as a fact: this long allegory is cut only where a counted formula or the plan's own naming puts a seam.
P03-022.strongest_rejected_alternative: The strongest alternative is to close at 16:50 and open a second row at 16:51, so that the Sodom comparison would stand apart from the Samaria comparison. It is weighed and not taken. On the alternative's far face the case is real - the witness records a samekh after MT 16:50 (single-witness), and the Sodom material is content-complete at that verse. On its near face it fails: MT 16:51 opens on the conjunction with Samaria, וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י (oshb:Ezek.16.51), the sister already named at 16:46, and MEASURED against every counted onset-formula class - word-event, messenger, son-of-man address, set-your-face, hand-of-YHWH, transport and dateline - that verse belongs to none (sweep: onset-class formulae at MT 16:51, 0 of 1 verse). A mark cannot supply the licensed onset the cut would need, so the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates while the comparison is carried on as one movement.
P03-022.device_notes: The single-witness apparatus across 16:44-16:58, disclosed in full: a Ketiv/Qere note at MT 16:47 (oshb:Ezek.16.47), where the running text reads the ketiv עשיתי in place of the Qere עָשִׂ֑ית; two such notes at MT 16:51 (oshb:Ezek.16.51) and three at MT 16:53 (oshb:Ezek.16.53), none of them used to argue this boundary; one paseq at MT 16:52 (oshb:Ezek.16.52), count-only and single-witness, with no intra-verse position claimed; an editors' note on a vowel reading at MT 16:54 (oshb:Ezek.16.54); and two parashah marks, a samekh after MT 16:50 and a samekh after MT 16:58, each single-witness. No further Ketiv/Qere note, paseq, editors' note or mark falls inside the span (sweep: 15 verses). The samekh after 16:50 is disclosed for the interior seam it corroborates rather than for this row's own edges; the one after 16:58 stands at the close. A second interior turn was weighed and not taken: the restoration named at 16:53 sits inside an ironic humiliation clause, “that you may bear your own shame” (web:Ezek.16.54), and carries no formula onset and no mark of its own.

P04-005.boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches the ch 20/21 numbering shift and is written dual. Onset: the strict word-event formula at web:Ezek.20.45 = oshb:Ezek.21.1 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר), a hard seam. MT 20:44 is followed by a pe (single-witness), corroborating the onset at MT 21:1. Close: web:Ezek.20.49 = oshb:Ezek.21.5 (וָאֹמַ֕ר אֲהָ֖הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֵ֚מָּה אֹמְרִ֣ים לִ֔י הֲלֹ֛א מְמַשֵּׁ֥ל מְשָׁלִ֖ים הֽוּא), the prophet's own outcry, rendered in web:Ezek.20.49 (= oshb:Ezek.21.5) as “Isn’t he a speaker of parables”. The verse names the mashal root, but a reported taunt in the prophet's own mouth is a turn in the account and no close-role formula, so the close's near face carries no licensed signal; a pe stands immediately after it (single-witness) and corroborates that paragraph only. That unlicensed close is what this row's reduced confidence rests on. That pe is also the point where the Masoretic tradition's own paragraph division sits exactly at the WEB's chapter break, so this zone is a seam site and a numbering site at once.
P04-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating web:Ezek.20.45-Ezek.21.5 = oshb:Ezek.21.1-Ezek.21.10 (the mashal plus its plain-sense restatement against the land) as one row was considered and rejected: web:Ezek.21.1 = oshb:Ezek.21.6 opens with its own strict word-event formula, a second hard seam, and the outcry at web:Ezek.20.49 = oshb:Ezek.21.5 already ends the mashal, with a pe standing after it (single-witness).

P04-008.boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches MT ch 21. The seam references are written dual; where the weighing cites the MT face alone, it carries that face's prefix. Onset: a strict word-event formula at web:Ezek.21.8 = oshb:Ezek.21.13 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר), a hard seam; the verse behind it, web:Ezek.21.7 = oshb:Ezek.21.12, ends on the utterance signature, verse-final, and carries a pe after it (single-witness), so that onset is two-faced. Close: the emphatic I-YHWH-have-spoken formula at web:Ezek.21.17 = oshb:Ezek.21.22 (וְגַם אֲנִ֗י אַכֶּ֤ה כַפִּי֙ אֶל כַּפִּ֔י וַהֲנִחֹתִ֖י חֲמָתִ֑י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי), with a pe immediately after. The poem's own refrains, sharpened and polished, the sword doubled and then tripled, run between the two; the one two-faced competing onset inside them, at web:Ezek.21.14 = oshb:Ezek.21.19, is weighed below and held as a paragraph. Both outer seams are top grade on both faces -- the word-event formula against the verse-final utterance and pe behind it, and the I-YHWH-have-spoken formula with its pe against the word-event formula at web:Ezek.21.18 = oshb:Ezek.21.23 past it -- and what holds this row at medium rather than high is that interior rival, which carries real evidence on both of its own faces.
P04-008.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a second time at web:Ezek.21.12 = oshb:Ezek.21.17, which the WEB renders “Cry and wail, son of man”, was considered and rejected. That verse carries the son-of-man address, one of the 93 verses in that class, and carries no word-event and no messenger formula; the WEB opens no paragraph at it, and translation lineation would not drive a boundary in any case. A further seam was weighed one verse later, from both sides. The verse closing at web:Ezek.21.13 = oshb:Ezek.21.18 ends on the utterance formula (נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה), “says the Lord Yahweh”, with a pe following it in this witness (single-witness); the next verse, web:Ezek.21.14 = oshb:Ezek.21.19, opens with the ve'attah, the and-you address “You therefore, son of man, prophesy” (וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֕א). Both sides carry real evidence: an utterance-formula close on one side of the seam and, on the other, the ve'attah, an onset-class device that brings the son-of-man address with it. That signature is verse-final, its verse being one of the 81 in the long utterance class, so the second condition - the verse before it ending on a verse-final close-role formula - is met on the bytes here. What carries the unit past the seam is the shape of the renewal: a ve'attah that renews the command to prophesy to the same addressee, standing after a verse-final utterance signature, is a paragraph and not an onset. The ve'attah is new at MT 21:19, but the address it renews is not: the son-of-man address with the command to prophesy already stands at web:Ezek.21.9 = oshb:Ezek.21.14, where it introduces the book's only messenger formula naming the Lord alone, כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֑י, and the son-of-man address returns at web:Ezek.21.12 = oshb:Ezek.21.17; and MT 21:19 continues the same sword doubled a third time (וְתִכָּפֵ֞ל חֶ֤רֶב שְׁלִישִׁ֨תָה֙, oshb:Ezek.21.19), the sword already sharpened and polished at oshb:Ezek.21.14-16, rather than opening a new topic.

P06-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: 25:12 opens with the messenger formula and a fresh addressee, "כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֣עַן עֲשׂ֥וֹת אֱד֛וֹם בִּנְקֹ֥ם נָקָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֶּאְשְׁמ֥וּ אָשׁ֖וֹם וְנִקְּמ֥וּ בָהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.12) — Edom — again a messenger-formula addressee-change cut. In the WEB, “Because Edom has dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and has greatly offended, and taken revenge on them,” (web:Ezek.25.12). Close (both sides): 25:14 ends "וְנָתַתִּ֨י אֶת נִקְמָתִ֜י בֶּאֱד֗וֹם בְּיַד֙ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעָשׂ֣וּ בֶאֱד֔וֹם כְּאַפִּ֖י וְכַחֲמָתִ֑י וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ אֶת נִקְמָתִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14), carrying a PE immediately after (single-witness). The close itself is a disclosed deviation from the strict recognition formula: the verb clause reads "and they shall know MY VENGEANCE" (an object noun, not "that I am YHWH"), stacked with the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature, "נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14); it belongs to the utterance list (sweep: 81 verses), not the strict recognition list (sweep: 28 verses) or either 2ms/2mp recognition family. Behind this row, 25:11 closed Moab on the strict 3mp recognition + SAMEKH (single-witness); ahead, 25:15 opens a fresh messenger formula with the addressee change to the Philistines. Both faces of both seams therefore carry signals the witness counts; what holds this row's confidence lower is the shape of the division itself, which the plan leaves open for these oracles — four short rows, two, or one seventeen-verse row — with this row standing as one of the four.
P06-003.device_notes: 25:14's close names "my vengeance" rather than the strict "that I am YHWH" recognition object, so it is cited here as an utterance-formula close with a recognition-adjacent variant, not quoted as the strict recognition formula. A second messenger formula stands inside the span at 25:13 (oshb:Ezek.25.13), where the therefore-turn opens the verdict against Edom; it is disclosed here and licenses no seam, since the addressee does not change and 25:12 does not end on a close-role formula.

P06-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:1 opens "וַיְהִ֛י בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1) — a year-and-day dateline whose month is not named (“In the eleventh year, in the first of the month”, web:Ezek.26.1, WEB) together with the PERFECT-form word-event, "הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1), the 7-verse hayah family the dated oracles use after their dateline, a HARD seam and the strongest onset class in the book. In the WEB, “In the eleventh year, in the first of the month, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.26.1). 26:2 supplies the accusation, "בֶּן אָדָ֗ם יַ֠עַן אֲשֶׁר אָ֨מְרָה צֹּ֤ר עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הֶאָ֔ח נִשְׁבְּרָ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעַמִּ֖ים נָסֵ֣בָּה אֵלָ֑י אִמָּלְאָ֖ה הָחֳרָֽבָה" (oshb:Ezek.26.2), quoting Tyre's own "Aha!" against Jerusalem. Close (both sides): 26:6 ends "וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּחֶ֖רֶב תֵּהָרַ֑גְנָה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.6), the strict 3mp recognition formula, with a PE immediately after (single-witness). Ahead, 26:7 reopens with a fresh messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר…", oshb:Ezek.26.7) introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege — a new speech unit against the same addressee, not an addressee change, which is why it is held as its own row rather than folded in here: the refrain at 26:6 closes THIS unit. The onset's far face is the mid-verse recognition at 25:17 rather than a verse-final close, and the plan flags this chapter among those where onset and close collide, holding four messenger units, one row per unit, as its default, so this row's confidence stays below what its close seam alone would carry.
P06-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating all of 26:1-21 as one row was rejected: the chapter reads as four independently marked units (1-6, 7-14, 15-18, 19-21), the first opened by its dateline and word-event and the other three by a messenger formula, each followed by a section mark in this witness (single-witness); the 26:6 recognition-formula-plus-PE close is independently marked and, since a refrain closes the unit before it, belongs to the unit before it, forcing 26:7 to open fresh.
P06-005.device_notes: 26:1's dateline is a hard seam but not a parent seam (the oracles-against-the-nations collection is nation-ordered, not date-ordered). 26:3 carries the “Behold, I am against you” (web:Ezek.26.3, WEB) verdict-onset idiom, הִנְנִ֥י (oshb:Ezek.26.3), disclosed as sub-onset corroboration, not a competing row onset. The internal four-way split of this chapter rests on the bespoke, disclosed rationale above rather than on a forced single reading.

P06-015.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:24 turns to Israel inside the Sidon word-event, וְלֹֽא יִהְיֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Ezek.28.24), and it does so with no formula device standing in the verse - the turn is carried by its content alone. The far face behind it ends verse-final on the strict recognition formula, וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.28.23), so a counted close sits behind an onset whose own near face carries no counted signal, and that unlicensed near face is the ground of this row's confidence. Close: 28:26 ends on the recognition formula with the their-God extension, וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.28.26), verse-final in effect because only the dependent apposition follows it, and a samekh is recorded after that verse (single-witness); its far face at 29:1 opens the tenth-year dateline with the perfect-form word-event (oshb:Ezek.29.1), so the close stands two-faced. One seam inside the span is licensed on both faces and weighed rather than taken: at 28:24/28:25 the messenger formula of 28:25 (oshb:Ezek.28.25) follows 28:24's verse-final recognition and the mark after it. It is held because cutting there would leave 28:24 alone as a one-verse remainder, and because the plan names 28:24-26 as the coda to Israel - the turn to Israel, the gathering promise and the settled dwelling, one restoration movement closed by the recognition at 28:26.
P06-015.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting this coda at 28:24/28:25 instead, so that a second row would open on the messenger formula, is the strongest alternative, and it is licensed on both faces: 28:24 ends verse-final on the adonai-form recognition, וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.28.24), with a samekh recorded after that verse (single-witness), and 28:25 opens on the messenger formula כֹּֽה אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.28.25), which that verse-final close licenses. It is weighed and not taken, on two stated grounds: taking it would leave 28:24 standing alone as a one-verse remainder, and the plan names 28:24-26 as the coda to Israel, one movement - the turn to Israel, the gathering promise and the settled dwelling - closed by the recognition at 28:26. The mark is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates.
P06-015.device_notes: The single-witness apparatus inside this span: a samekh recorded after MT 28:24 (oshb:Ezek.28.24) and another after MT 28:26 (oshb:Ezek.28.26), and one paseq inside MT 28:25 (oshb:Ezek.28.25), count-only with no intra-verse position claimed. No Ketiv/Qere and no editors' note falls in the span (sweep: 3 verses). The samekh after 28:24 is disclosed for the interior seam it corroborates rather than for the onset at the head of this span. A wider alternative was weighed and refused on the plan's naming of 28:24-26 as the coda: folding these three verses back into the Sidon oracle at oshb:Ezek.28.20-Ezek.28.23 would dissolve this row's own onset seam, where MT 28:23 ends verse-final on the strict recognition formula that closes the Sidon verdict and 28:24 turns from the city to Israel's house. This coda closes the stretch of oracles against the nations that runs from chapter 25 through chapter 28 and still belongs to that collection; the next dateline seam stands outside the span at oshb:Ezek.29.1.

P09-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split between the stick demonstration and its interpretation, e.g. after web:Ezek.37.20 (“The sticks on which you write will be in your hand before their eyes.” (web:Ezek.37.20)) or after web:Ezek.37.23 (the purification promise). Rejected: reading each section mark as standing on the verse it follows, no samekh or pe falls in this row's INTERIOR, oshb:Ezek.37.15-Ezek.37.27, single-witness. The only marks anywhere in range are the pe recorded on 37.14, behind the onset seam, and the samekh recorded on 37.28, at the close seam. The messenger-formula reopenings at oshb:Ezek.37.19 and oshb:Ezek.37.21 keep the same hearers, and a messenger formula opens a sub-unit only where the addressee changes or where the verse before it ends on a close-role formula: 37:18 and 37:20 end on no formula of any counted class, so neither condition is met here.
P09-002.device_notes: Category disclosure: the oshb:Ezek.37.15-Ezek.37.28 span is anchored as a sign-act (the commanded stick action of oshb:Ezek.37.16-Ezek.37.20), but its interpretation at oshb:Ezek.37.21-Ezek.37.28 carries the salvation-oracle burden (gather/return, the covenant of peace at oshb:Ezek.37.26, ‘my servant David’ and ‘my sanctuary’ devices) -- a one-clause category deviation rather than a split: the pe behind it at oshb:Ezek.37.14 and the samekh closing it at oshb:Ezek.37.28 are the row's only framing marks, and the addressee stays constant across both halves. oshb:Ezek.37.16 is a doubled ketiv/qere verse: two notes on one verse, each written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.16, ketiv), and each read as the same consonantal word under different pointing -- the first note reads חֲבֵרָ֑יו and the second חֲבֵרָֽיו, the two differing by exactly one codepoint, U+0591 HEBREW ACCENT ETNAHTA in the first against U+05BD HEBREW POINT METEG in the second (MEASURED by comparing the two readings the K/Q apparatus gives at this verse, codepoint by codepoint; WLC/OSHB, single witness), and 37.19 carries one further note on the same word (written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, ketiv), read חֲבֵרָ֑יו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, Qere)); 37.22 carries a further K/Q note in this span (written יהיה (oshb:Ezek.37.22, ketiv), read יִֽהְיוּ (oshb:Ezek.37.22, Qere)). A boundary is never argued from any of these Qere readings; they are disclosed as textual-variant sites only.

P10-008.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 41:12 turns to a different structure from the side-chamber circuit just closed, a change of measured object rather than a bare topic shift: וְהַבִּנְיָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֶל פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה פְּאַ֣ת דֶּֽרֶךְ הַיָּ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.41.12) “The building that was before the separate place at the side toward the west” (web:Ezek.41.12), confirmed by the fresh measuring verb וּמָדַ֣ד אֶת הַבַּ֔יִת (oshb:Ezek.41.13) that opens this row's own accounting of the building. The row carries the temple/separate-place/building triad each measured at a hundred cubits (41:13-14), the rear building and its galleries with a K/Q lexical variant on 'galleries' at oshb:Ezek.41.15 (ואתוקיהא, checked: a form variant, not a numeral), the side-chamber gallery structure (41:16-19), the cherubim-and-palm-tree decorative program running to above the entrance (41:18-20), the doorposts of the nave (41:21), the wooden altar-table with its own speak-formula notice, וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֚ה הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.41.22), its speech rendered “This is the table that is before Yahweh” (web:Ezek.41.22), opened by the 'spoke to me' root, distinct from the 'said to me' form at 41:4, the double doors of the nave and sanctuary (41:23-25), and the repeated cherubim-and-palm-tree pattern closing on the porch threshold. Close side: 41:26 ends וְצַלְע֥וֹת הַבַּ֖יִת וְהָעֻבִּֽים (oshb:Ezek.41.26), “the side rooms of the temple and the thresholds” (web:Ezek.41.26), and the next verse, oshb:Ezek.42.1, moves the tour out to the outer court with its double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי … וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי -- a strong close by contrast, since the following onset carries the counted double-transport device even though this row's own onset rests on the measured-object change rather than a formula. The puncta extraordinaria at 41:20, וְקִ֖יר הַׄהֵׄיׄכָֽׄלׄ (oshb:Ezek.41.20), five instances of the upper dot U+05C4, are disclosed single-witness as intra-row texture on the decorative program's own close, not as boundary evidence.

P10-010.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:1 opens with a double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה ... וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.1) “he brought me out into the outer court” (web:Ezek.42.1) ... “Then he brought me into the room” (web:Ezek.42.1) -- the strongest onset in the span after 40:1 and 43:1 -- moving the tour to the priests' chambers, first north-side (42:1-9) then, by parallel description, south-side (42:10-12). Close side: 42:13-14 supplies the row's function. The guide's naming speech closes the survey of these rooms by reading and not by formula: the וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) it carries is an onset-type device inside the vision, weighed below, and no close formula at all. These are the holy chambers where the priests “eat the most holy things” (web:Ezek.42.13) and must change garments before approaching the people -- a law-toned close inside a measurement row, disclosed rather than reclassified. The double transport at the onset is a licensed onset inside the vision, a stronger opening than a bare content shift would give; the close rests on the reading above rather than on a formula, and no parashah mark stands anywhere in these chapters to corroborate either edge (single-witness).
P10-010.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 42:12/42:13, where the guide's own וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) stands at the verse's head, was weighed and not taken. Inside a vision that speech is a licensed onset whoever speaks it, so the rival's near face carries a real signal; its far face, 42:12, ends on the doors of the south-side rooms with no close-role formula, and neither verse carries a section mark (single-witness). What holds the row against it is that 42:13-14 states the function of the very chambers just measured, so the naming speech completes this survey rather than opening a new one, and taking the cut would leave a two-verse remainder that is no unit of its own.
P10-010.device_notes: No parashah mark in ch 42. Two K/Q verses disclosed (42:9 doubled, 42:14 single), both checked: neither touches a numeral. Content disclosure, not a category deviation: 42:13-14 states a food-purity law for the chambers just measured; the row is classed as a temple measurement because the chamber dimensions (42:1-12) dominate it and the law clause closes rather than opens the unit. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: three occurrences over two verses (42:10, and two on 42:13); where each stroke stands inside its verse is not available from this witness. P02-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.22 וַיִּשְׂא֤וּ הַכְּרוּבִים֙ אֶת כַּנְפֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וּכְב֧וֹד אֱלֹהֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מִלְמָֽעְלָה resumes the vision frame exactly where 11:13 left it (the cherubim and wheels, last seen departing the city at 10:19) - a change of scene that no onset device carries on this near face, which is the ground on which this row's confidence stands below the middle of the scale. P03-023.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.17.11 opens on the word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.17.11), and its near face is licensed by that formula alone. P03-023.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this span at the 17:18/17:19 seam, so that the interpretation (17:11-18) and the sworn verdict (17:19-21) stand as two rows, is the strongest alternative here, and it is weighed on both faces. P04-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: the dateline at oshb:Ezek.20.1 (וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗ית בַּֽחֲמִשִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ בָּ֧אוּ אֲנָשִׁ֛ים מִזִּקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לִדְרֹ֣שׁ אֶת יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ לְפָנָֽי, the elders come to inquire) opens a narrative frame without its own word-event; the strict word-event formula follows immediately at oshb:Ezek.20.2 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר) as the oracle's sub-onset inside that frame. A pe follows MT 19:14 (single witness), the paragraph mark standing behind this unit's onset at MT 20:1. Close: oshb:Ezek.20.26 (וָאֲטַמֵּ֤א אוֹתָם֙ בְּמַתְּנוֹתָ֔ם בְּהַעֲבִ֖יר כָּל פֶּ֣טֶר רָ֑חַם לְמַ֣עַן אֲשִׁמֵּ֔ם לְמַ֨עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵֽדְע֔וּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה) ends the third narrated generation's indictment and carries a samekh, immediately followed by a fresh therefore-plus-messenger-formula onset at oshb:Ezek.20.27. Nothing formula-marked interrupts the recitation between the two onsets: the recurring for-my-name's-sake clauses at oshb:Ezek.20.9, 20.14 and 20.22, and the two Sabbath-gift notices, are content-level structuring devices, not messenger-formula or word-event onsets, so the counted onset formulae support one row across all three narrated generations (Egypt, the first wilderness generation, and the children) rather than a formula-marked internal cut. The oath embedded in oshb:Ezek.20.3 (בֶּן אָדָ֗ם דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶת זִקְנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הֲלִדְרֹ֥שׁ אֹתִ֖י אַתֶּ֣ם בָּאִ֑ים חַי אָ֨נִי֙ אִם אִדָּרֵ֣שׁ לָכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה) and the utterance formula there are paragraph-internal texture, not a competing close.
P04-001.device_notes: 26 verses in one row, against the 7-10 verse target: the length is disclosed as a fact and is no ground for the grade, which rests on the faces. The close near face at oshb:Ezek.20.26 ends on a recognition-shaped clause that the counted recognition families do not include, with a samekh after it (single witness) that corroborates and decides nothing, while the onset near face at oshb:Ezek.20.1 carries the dateline and the word-event follows at 20:2; no formula-supported split stands inside the recitation; count-only paseq (single-witness) at oshb:Ezek.20.1, intra-verse position unsourceable; identity numbering throughout this row (outside the ch 20/21 shift).

P06-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: 25:1 opens with the word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.25.1) — the strict 39-form and the 41-verse vayehi-any both, carrying no dateline. In the WEB, “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.25.1). 25:2 supplies the addressee, "בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.2) — the set-your-face command “toward the children of Ammon” (web:Ezek.25.2, WEB) is the first of the book's set-your-face verses (sweep: 9 verses) to name a foreign nation, and the class shift that opens the oracles-against-the-nations collection; Ammon itself is not a new addressee here, since the sword oracle at MT 21:33 (= WEB 21:28) already concerns the children of Ammon. Close (weighed from both sides): 25:7 ends "לָכֵ֡ן הִנְנִי֩ נָטִ֨יתִי אֶת יָדִ֜י עָלֶ֗יךָ וּנְתַתִּ֤יךָֽ לבג לַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִן הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֖יךָ מִן הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת אַשְׁמִ֣ידְךָ֔ וְיָדַעְתָּ֖ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.7; לבג there is the verse’s ketiv, Qere לְבַז֙), closing on the 2ms recognition variant "and you shall know that I am YHWH" with a SAMEKH immediately after. An earlier internal close sits at 25:5, "וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת רַבָּה֙ לִנְוֵ֣ה גְמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן לְמִרְבַּץ צֹ֑אן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.5), which also ends on a 2mp recognition-family clause (the wider 2mp recognition family, sweep: 21 verses, includes 25:5, not the 2s list, sweep: 5 verses (gender unresolved on the skeleton)) and carries its own SAMEKH. Because a refrain closes the unit before it, both 25:5 and 25:7 are treated as closes; they are kept in one row because 25:6 reopens with a coordinating messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה", oshb:Ezek.25.6) against the same addressee (Ammon) rather than a fresh nation, so no addressee-class shift separates 25:5 from 25:7. The 25:5/25:6 seam is therefore a licensed rival carrying a signal on both of its faces - the coordinating messenger formula on its near face at 25:6, and on its far face a verse-final recognition-family clause at 25:5 with a samekh after it (single witness) - and it is held on the stated ground that the addressee does not change; that held rival is what places this row's confidence at the middle of the scale. P06-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at the internal 25:5/25:6 seam into two rows (25:1-5 and 25:6-7) was rejected: 25:5 does carry its own SAMEKH (single-witness) and a recognition-family close, and the messenger formula at 25:6 makes the rival licensed and two-faced, but 25:6 reopens against the same addressee with no set-your-face or word-event onset of its own, and a resulting 25:6-7 row would be two verses carrying only that coordinating messenger formula, with no complete word-event unit to hold it.
P06-001.device_notes: Category anchor: 25:1-7 carries the addressee-class shift onto a foreign nation (set-your-face at 25:2) that anchors it as an oracle against a nation. P08-015.boundary_rationale: Onset: a messenger formula with an addressee change opens a fresh sub-unit at Ezek.34.17 וְאַתֵּ֣נָה צֹאנִ֔י כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הִנְנִ֤י שֹׁפֵט֙ בֵּֽין שֶׂ֣ה לָשֶׂ֔ה לָאֵילִ֖ים וְלָעַתּוּדִֽים (oshb:Ezek.34.17), turning to address 'my flock' directly (second-feminine-plural, distinct from the shepherds indicted in Ezek.34.1-Ezek.34.16) — the addressee-change licence for a messenger-formula cut. A second messenger formula follows at Ezek.34.20 לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם הִנְנִי אָ֕נִי וְשָֽׁפַטְתִּי֙ בֵּֽין שֶׂ֣ה בִרְיָ֔ה וּבֵ֥ין שֶׂ֖ה רָזָֽה (oshb:Ezek.34.20), after a samekh mark (single witness) following Ezek.34.19 וְצֹאנִ֑י מִרְמַ֤ס רַגְלֵיכֶם֙ תִּרְעֶ֔ינָה וּמִרְפַּ֥שׂ רַגְלֵיכֶ֖ם תִּשְׁתֶּֽינָה (oshb:Ezek.34.19); disclosed as paragraph-internal, not row-final, since the judgment between fat and lean sheep opens directly into the 'one shepherd' promise. The emphatic close “I, Yahweh, have spoken” (web:Ezek.34.24) follows at Ezek.34.24 וַאֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֶהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים וְעַבְדִּ֥י דָוִ֖ד נָשִׂ֣יא בְתוֹכָ֑ם אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.34.24), disclosed as an internal emphatic close, not final, since the covenant-of-peace material continues through Ezek.34.25-Ezek.34.30. A recognition formula closes that material at Ezek.34.27 וְנָתַן֩ עֵ֨ץ הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה אֶת פִּרְי֗וֹ וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ תִּתֵּ֣ן יְבוּלָ֔הּ וְהָי֥וּ עַל אַדְמָתָ֖ם לָבֶ֑טַח וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כִּי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בְּשִׁבְרִי֙ אֶת מֹט֣וֹת עֻלָּ֔ם וְהִ֨צַּלְתִּ֔ים מִיַּ֖ד הָעֹבְדִ֥ים בָּהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.34.27) and again at Ezek.34.30 וְיָדְע֗וּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם אִתָּ֑ם וְהֵ֗מָּה עַמִּי֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.34.30), both disclosed as paragraph-final rather than row-final, since Ezek.34.31 restates the covenant formula once more. Close: the utterance formula at Ezek.34.31 וְאַתֵּ֥ן צֹאנִ֛י צֹ֥אן מַרְעִיתִ֖י אָדָ֣ם אַתֶּ֑ם אֲנִי֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.34.31) plus a pe mark (single witness) close this row, immediately before the fresh word-event of Ezek.35.1. Both seams weighed: the onset at 34:17 turns the address to the flock and is licensed there, standing after Ezek.34.16, which carries no close-role formula; the close is two-faced, its utterance formula answered across the seam by the fresh word-event of Ezek.35.1. This chapter is one the book's own division holds together as a single unit, with the cut at 34:17 as its disclosed alternative, and that open question is what keeps this row's confidence below the middle of the scale.

P10-006.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:48, one of the counted transport verses (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), opens with וַיְבִאֵנִי֮ אֶל אֻלָ֣ם הַבַּיִת֒ (oshb:Ezek.40.48) “he brought me to the porch of the house” (web:Ezek.40.48), marking entry into the temple building proper, distinct from every court and gate measured before it. A second transport verb follows at 41:1, וַיְבִיאֵ֖נִי אֶל הַהֵיכָ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.41.1) “He brought me to the nave and measured” (web:Ezek.41.1), disclosed here as continuous forward motion through one threshold sequence rather than a fresh row seam, since no formula or refrain close intervenes between the porch and the nave. The two-verse porch description (40:48-49) is held with the four-verse nave description (41:1-4) as one row rather than left as an under-three-verse fragment. Close side: 41:4 ends with וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֖ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים (oshb:Ezek.41.4) “He said to me,” then “This is the most holy place” (web:Ezek.41.4), the guide's naming of the room, which closes the survey of it by reading; the he-said-to-me that naming carries is an onset-type device inside the vision and not a close formula; 41:5's fresh measuring verb then turns to a new object, the house wall. This close therefore rests on a reading of the guide's speech and not on a counted close-role formula.
P10-006.strongest_rejected_alternative: Leaving 40:48-49 as its own two-verse row was rejected as a two-verse fragment; splitting porch from nave at 41:1 was also weighed, since 41:1's transport verb is itself a counted guided-motion verse, but no close-grade device stands between 40:49 and 41:1 to justify the cut, whereas 41:4 supplies the guide's naming.

The naming speech at 41:4 uses a distinct root from the 'he spoke to me' forms at 40:4 and 40:45, both the man's own speech and neither among the book-wide sweep counts cited here. P10-015.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:18 opens on a said-to-me verse, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י, and then carries בֶּן אָדָם֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.43.18) 'son of man, thus says the Lord YHWH' -- one of the book's 122 messenger-formula verses, and the clearest speech-onset here after the throne declaration of 43:1-9 -- introducing the altar's dedication ordinances. The utterance formula נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.43.19) stands inside 43:19, embedded between the relative clause about the priests near to me and the infinitive that follows it, so it closes nothing there, neither a paragraph nor the row, and the seven-day consecration instructions run on. The row carries the young-bull sin offering, the blood rite on the horns and corners, the second-day goat, the seven-day consecration, and closes at 43:27 on the same utterance formula, וְרָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.43.27) “Then I will accept you,’ says the Lord Yahweh” (web:Ezek.43.27), this time genuinely row-final. Close side: immediately after that utterance the verse carries two consecutive samekh marks, the sole doubled occurrence among the book's marked verses (sweep: 183 verses), single witness -- the close rests first on that verse-final utterance formula, with the doubled mark standing behind it as corroboration. Both sides converge unusually cleanly here: a messenger-formula onset opposite an utterance-plus-doubled-mark close.

P11-002.boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.44.5 opens with a son-of-man address launching an instructional mode; 44.6 and 44.9 both carry the messenger formula, addressed throughout to the same topic (the house of Israel's abominations in admitting uncircumcised foreigners to the sanctuary) with no addressee-class change between them, so neither reopens the row on its own. The unit turns at 44.10 to the Levites' judgment for their prior idolatry: they may minister but may not approach as priests, with the utterance signature appearing mid-paragraph at 44.12 (paragraph-final, not row-final, since no fresh onset follows immediately) and the paragraph closing at 44.14. Close: Ezek.44.14 closes on content — the Levites set as keepers of the house's charge — with no close-role formula of its own, and the pe parashah mark recorded after Ezek.44.14 (single-witness) corroborates that close without supplying one, so that near face is the ground on which this row is held at reduced confidence; the very next verse, 44.15, turns to a different priestly class (the sons of Zadok) with its own utterance signature standing verse-final at its end -- an addressee-class shift inside the same law section.
P11-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 44.9/44.10 (foreigner law versus the Levites' judgment), since 44.9 is itself a messenger-formula restatement. Weighed on both faces: the near face, Ezek.44.10, opens the Levites' judgment with no onset formula of its own, and the far face, Ezek.44.9, restates the messenger formula without ending on a close-role formula, so the rival is unlicensed on the face that would carry it. Rejected because no addressee-class change occurs there -- both halves concern the same reform of sanctuary access -- and no parashah or refrain marks that point, while the pe after 44.14 (single witness) corroborates this row's own close instead.

P11-009.boundary_rationale: Onset: a transport verb at Ezek.46.19 (“he brought me through the entry” (web:Ezek.46.19) ... “into the holy rooms for the priests” (web:Ezek.46.19)) reopens the vision at the hard seam at Ezek.46.18/46.19, a shift from temple-law material to a guided vision scene. The row covers the priests' kitchens inside the sanctuary (19-20) and a further transport (“he brought me out into the outer court” (web:Ezek.46.21), 21) to the four corner courts and their boiling places for the people's sacrifices (21-24). A samekh mark is recorded after Ezek.46.19 itself (single-witness) -- one verse INTO this row, not at its outer boundary -- disclosed as mid-unit texture that does not cut, since the transport-and-explanation sequence at 46.19-20 reads as one scene. Close: the chapter ends at 46.24, which opens on וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Ezek.46.24), the guide's 'he said to me' -- an onset-type device inside the vision, not a close-role formula -- so the close near face carries no counted close signal, and that is the ground on which this row is held at reduced confidence; the next hard seam is at Ezek.46.24/47.1, where the river vision opens with its own transport verb -- one guided vision scene running on into another rather than a change of material, but still a hard seam this row's span does not cross.
P11-009.device_notes: MT 46.22 carries seven U+05C4 puncta-extraordinaria combining marks in the verse's own bytes, single-witness. A row splicing this verse carries the marks in its own quoted bytes -- that is source-true, not degradation, and U+05C4 is treated as a legitimate combining mark, not corruption. The book's transport-verb sweep (sweep: 33 verses) names two verses in this chapter, both inside this row: Ezek.46.19, and Ezek.46.21, which carries two guided-motion verbs, the first of them verse-initial, וַיּוֹצִיאֵ֗נִי and וַיַּ֣עֲבִירֵ֔נִי (oshb:Ezek.46.21), 'he brought me out ... and made me pass', an intra-row transport sub-onset that does not cut. The samekh recorded after Ezek.46.19 is single-witness, mid-unit, non-cutting: a cut at 46.19/46.20 was weighed and not taken, and it is not a mark-only candidate -- 46:20 opens with 'he said to me', an onset-type device inside the vision, and the samekh corroborates it -- but it is refused because it would leave 46.19 as a one-verse row. The same speech device opens 46.24, this row's own last verse, and a cut at 46.23/46.24 is refused on the same ground.

P01-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:12 וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ (oshb:Ezek.3.12) (“Then the Spirit lifted me up” (web:Ezek.3.12)) begins the return-transport away from the plain-vision back to the exiles, distinct in texture from the preceding commissioning speech (no address, no imperative - narrated action). 3:14 carries the hand-of-YHWH construct, וְיַד יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה (oshb:Ezek.3.14) ('the hand of YHWH was strong upon me'), and the same verse carries the transport clause, so, like the onset verse, it stands among the counted transport verses; it is not read as a fresh vision onset here, in contrast to 1:3 and 3:22 - it sits inside a single continuous journey (lifted up → went in bitterness → came to Tel-abib) with no scene change around it, so it is weighed as a licensed rival and held, as the rejected alternative states. Close: 3:15, וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.3.15) (“I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days” (web:Ezek.3.15)); no parashah mark is recorded at 3:15 (single-witness), which is not read as counterevidence against the seam. The gap this closes is temporal, not formulaic: 3:16 reopens on “At the end of seven days” (web:Ezek.3.16) with its own strict word-event. What the two seams come to is this: the close near face at 3:15 is the arrival that completes the return movement this row reports, a close in the composition's own voice, and its far face at 3:16 carries the strict word-event; the onset near face at 3:12 carries the transport verb, while its far face 3:11 ends on the sending instruction (oshb:Ezek.3.11) with no close-role formula and no mark (single-witness); and the licensed rival at 3:13/3:14 is weighed and held on the two grounds stated below. That is the strength this row's boundary evidence comes to.
P01-005.device_notes: Hand-of-YHWH at 3:14 is one of the book's 7 verses carrying the construct, and it is weighed here as a licensed rival and held rather than taken as a hard seam (contrast the unit-opening uses at 1:3 and 3:22). K/Q at 3:15 checked before quoting: the unit's own splice above reads the qere form. Paseq at 3:13 disclosed count-only, single-witness.
P01-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: A cut at 3:13/3:14 is the live rival, weighed here face by face and not taken. Its near face, 3:14, carries two candidate drivers at once: the transport clause וְר֥וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֖תְנִי וַתִּקָּחֵ֑נִי (oshb:Ezek.3.14), which places 3:14, like the onset verse 3:12, among the transport verses the book counts (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), and the hand-of-YHWH construct, which could be read as a fresh vision onset. Its far face, 3:13, is the sound of the creatures' wings and wheels, with no close-role formula and no parashah mark recorded on it (single-witness). Because a transport verb licenses a seam, the rival is not dismissed; it is held on two stated grounds. A row under three verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and this cut would leave 3:12-13 and 3:14-15 as rows of two verses each, neither of them such a unit. And no scene change accompanies it: the same journey that begins at 3:12 continues without interruption through 3:15, so treating every occurrence of the construct as onset-grade would read a rival this single journey holds as a hard seam.

P01-006.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:16 carries the book's first strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.3.16)), a hard seam, since a strict word-event opens a new oracle and no unit runs across one (3:16 is one of the 39 strict-form verses and one of the 48 in the first-person family). A pe is recorded after this verse (single-witness); this witness's section marks carry no intra-verse position, so no claim is made about where within or after 3:16 the mark stands, ahead of 3:17's watchman charge, צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.3.17) (“I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.3.17)). A samekh follows 3:19 (single-witness), between the wicked-man case (3:18-19) and the righteous-man case (3:20-21); disclosed as an internal paragraph mark, not a unit cut, since both cases are one paired illustration of the same watchman charge and no fresh onset device stands at 3:20. Close: 3:21, whose last clause turns back on the prophet himself, וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶֽת נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ (oshb:Ezek.3.21), a discourse close the counted close-role forms do not carry; the second samekh stands after that verse (single-witness) and the hand-of-YHWH reopens the scene at 3:22 (oshb:Ezek.3.22) on the far side. The close near face therefore carries a reader-found refrain and no counted formula, and that is the ground of the confidence this row records.

P01-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: 6:1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.6.1), “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.6.1), a strict word-event, hard seam. 6:2 opens the oracle's direction with שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.6.2) (“set your face toward the mountains of Israel” (web:Ezek.6.2)). A 2mp recognition-family close occurs mid-unit at 6:7, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.6.7) ('and you shall know that I am Yahweh'); it is disclosed but read as paragraph-final rather than unit-final, since 6:8 continues without a fresh onset device (“Yet I will leave a remnant” (web:Ezek.6.8)). Close: 6:10, the strict recognition formula וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.6.10) ('and they shall know that I am Yahweh'), with a pe recorded after it (single-witness), immediately before a fresh messenger formula reopens the address at 6:11. That formula does not stand verse-final: לֹ֤א אֶל חִנָּם֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי follows it inside the same verse (oshb:Ezek.6.10), a finite clause with no subordinator, so the close near face carries a formula the verse runs on past - the weaker near-face shape that grounds the confidence this row records, while its far face at 6:11 carries the messenger formula.

P02-019.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.14.1 וַיָּב֤וֹא אֵלַי֙ אֲנָשִׁ֔ים מִזִּקְנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ לְפָנָֽי — “Then some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat before me.” (web:Ezek.14.1) — is a bare narrative scene-opener with no formula; a pe follows this very verse (single-witness), and the word-event formula proper opens the next verse, oshb:Ezek.14.2 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר. Behind the onset, MT 13:23 ends on the second-person feminine-plural recognition refrain (sweep: 64 verses) and carries no mark (single-witness), so this onset has a close-role signal on its far face while its own near face carries no device. The row opens at 14:1 rather than 14:2 because the elders' scene-setting is what the oracle answers (“Should I be inquired of at all by them?” (web:Ezek.14.3)). Close: oshb:Ezek.14.11 לְ֠מַעַן לֹֽא יִתְע֨וּ ע֤וֹד בֵּֽית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאַֽחֲרַ֔י וְלֹֽא יִטַּמְּא֥וּ ע֖וֹד בְּכָל פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֑ם וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֣י לְעָ֗ם וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה; a second pe follows this verse (single-witness), so this witness records a pe on both the first and the last verse of the row, and only the second of them stands at a seam. P02-019.device_notes: K/Q at oshb:Ezek.14.4 is disclosed above; paseq at 14.4 and 14.6 is count-only, single-witness. P05-007.boundary_rationale: Onset: 24:1 is a HARD SEAM — the siege dateline, the 5th of the 14 oracle datelines in canonical order (1:1, 1:2, 8:1, 20:1, 24:1, 26:1, 29:1, 29:17, 30:20, 31:1, 32:1, 32:17, 33:21, 40:1) — and simultaneously the word-event formula with the date infixed between the word for "to me" and the word for "saying": present in the 41-verse vayehi-any word-event count and ABSENT from the strict 39-verse count (the infix breaks the adjacency the strict form requires). Whole verse = "וַיְהִי֩ דְבַר יְהוָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בַּשָּׁנָ֤ה הַתְּשִׁיעִית֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֔י בֶּעָשׂ֥וֹר לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.24.1)". Close: 24:14 stacks TWO close-grade formulae on one verse — the emphatic "I, YHWH, have spoken" (sweep: 14 verses) and the utterance formula (sweep: 81 verses) — whole verse = "אֲנִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ בָּאָ֣ה וְעָשִׂ֔יתִי לֹֽא אֶפְרַ֥ע וְלֹא אָח֖וּס וְלֹ֣א אֶנָּחֵ֑ם כִּדְרָכַ֤יִךְ וְכַעֲלִילוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ שְׁפָט֔וּךְ נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.24.14)".
P05-007.device_notes: Dateline 24:1 counted among the book's 14 oracle datelines and in the 41-verse vayehi-any word-event count; ABSENT from the strict 39-verse count because the year-month-day clause infixes between the two adjacency-anchor words the strict pattern requires; the 39/41/48/49-verse word-event counts are never blended. A single ketiv/qere pair sits at 24:2, its Qere reserved to the note layer rather than quoted here. Paseq at 24:6 (count-only, single-witness, unsourceable intra-verse position). Category deviation, in one sentence: the mashal label at 24:3 anchors this row as a spoken parable rather than a plain judgment speech.
P05-007.strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives were weighed for MT 24:1, and a third inside the row. (1) Treating 24:1-27 as ONE unit (24:1 as the head of this collection's entire last movement, no further internal cut) — rejected because 24:15 carries its own full-form strict word-event onset (a hard seam in its own right) and a genre shift from mashal to sign-act, and both halves carry independent formula closes (24:14 and 24:27); the resulting row would also run well past the 7-10 verse target, which is disclosed here and is no ground of its own. (2) Treating 24:1 as its OWN one-verse dated complex, separate from 24:2-14 — rejected because a dateline fused with a word-event in one verse is treated as a single onset that never splits, and because the day-naming command stands at 24:2, “write the name of the day, this same day” (web:Ezek.24.2), with the mashal's own opening command following at 24:3 (verse-final words "שְׁפֹ֔ת וְגַם יְצֹ֥ק בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם (oshb:Ezek.24.3)"), so the parable runs straight on from the date with no seam between them. (3) Cutting at 24:8/24:9 - the alternative the Masoretic paragraph layer proposes, named and weighed here. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 24:9 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.24.9). What its far face carries: MEASURED, the witness records a PE (petuchah, open section, single-witness) after MT 24:8 - and nothing else, because MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness MT 24:8 ends on a purpose infinitive (oshb:Ezek.24.8), with no utterance, recognition or I-YHWH-have-spoken signature anywhere in that verse. Whether it is licensed: it is NOT, since a messenger formula cuts only through a change of addressee or a close-role formula ending the verse before it. The first fails, because the addressee does not change - MT 24:6 already addresses the bloody city (oshb:Ezek.24.6) and MT 24:9 addresses that same city. The second fails, because the verse immediately before it does not END on a close-role formula, and a mark alone never supplies one. The stated ground on which this row holds: a section mark ranks below any licensed text signal, so the PE after MT 24:8 is weak corroboration, disclosed FOR the alternative it corroborates and not for this row, and it is outranked by the licensed drivers this row does rest on - the fused dateline-plus-word-event onset at 24:1 and the stacked I-YHWH-have-spoken plus utterance close at 24:14. So the 24:8/24:9 cut is an unlicensed rival with one face only: its near face carries the messenger formula measured above and nothing licenses it, and its far face carries the section mark (single-witness) and no close-role formula. It is paragraph-grade - weighed, disclosed and held - and, being unlicensed and one-faced, never fatal to the confidence this row carries.

Samekh at 24:27 (single-witness) is both this unit's close and the parent collection's own close. MEASURED in this witness, which records a mark on the verse it follows: a PE (petuchah, OPEN section, single-witness) stands on MT 24:14, behind this row's ONSET seam at 24:14/24:15; a samekh (single-witness) stands on MT 24:24, at the weighed rival's own seam; and a samekh (single-witness) stands on MT 24:27, this row's last verse. The sign word at 24:24 (oshb:Ezek.24.24) is what fixes this unit as an enacted sign. A licensed text signal outranks a section mark, so the PE is weak corroboration; this onset rests on the full-form strict word-event formula at 24:15.
P05-008.strongest_rejected_alternative: The rival is a cut at 24:24/24:25, and both sides of that seam carry evidence. Before it, 24:24 ends on a recognition clause of the counted adonai-form class (sweep: 5 verses), verse-final words וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.24.24), 2mp, the same form that closes 23:49, and this witness records a samekh after that verse (single-witness), which is entered as support for the rival. After it, 24:25 opens with the and-you-son-of-man address וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם (oshb:Ezek.24.25), one of the book's son-of-man verses (sweep: 93 verses) - and that address is the onset-class device the rival's licence rests on, since it turns the address from the house of Israel spoken to in the second person plural through 24:21-24 to the prophet himself, while 24:24 ends verse-final on the adonai-form recognition; no word-event formula, messenger formula, transport verb or dateline stands there. The cut is not taken because the sign word frames the verses that follow it: 24:24 names Ezekiel a sign, לְמוֹפֵ֔ת (oshb:Ezek.24.24), and 24:27 repeats the same word, לְמוֹפֵ֔ת (oshb:Ezek.24.27), for the prophet whose mouth will be opened, so 24:25-27 is the fulfilment the sign-act itself sets up and closes inside that inclusio rather than opening a unit of its own.
