P06-007.boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:15 opens with the messenger formula addressed "to Tyre", "כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה לְצ֑וֹר הֲלֹ֣א מִקּ֣וֹל מַפַּלְתֵּ֗ךְ בֶּאֱנֹ֨ק חָלָ֜ל בֵּהָ֤רֵֽג הֶ֨רֶג֙ בְּתוֹכֵ֔ךְ יִרְעֲשׁ֖וּ הָאִיִּֽים" (oshb:Ezek.26.15), reopening after the stacked "I YHWH have spoken" + utterance close and SAMEKH at 26:14. In the WEB, “The Lord Yahweh says to Tyre: ‘Won’t the islands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan, when the slaughter is made within you?” (web:Ezek.26.15). 26:17 embeds the noun "וְנָשְׂא֨וּ עָלַ֤יִךְ קִינָה֙ וְאָ֣מְרוּ לָ֔ךְ אֵ֣יךְ אָבַ֔דְתְּ נוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת מִיַּמִּ֑ים הָעִ֣יר הַהֻלָּ֗לָה אֲשֶׁר֩ הָיְתָ֨ה חֲזָקָ֤ה בַיָּם֙ הִ֣יא וְיֹשְׁבֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁר נָתְנ֥וּ חִתִּיתָ֖ם לְכָל יוֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ" (oshb:Ezek.26.17), "lamentation/qinah" — but as REPORTED future speech the sea-princes will voice ("they shall take up a qinah over you"), not a command to the prophet; disclosed here as texture, not treated as a lament_qinah onset. 26:18 ends "עַתָּה֙ יֶחְרְד֣וּ הָֽאִיִּ֔ן י֖וֹם מַפַּלְתֵּ֑ךְ וְנִבְהֲל֛וּ הָאִיִּ֥ים אֲשֶׁר בַּיָּ֖ם מִצֵּאתֵֽךְ" (oshb:Ezek.26.18) with NO recognition, utterance, or "I YHWH have spoken" formula in the verse; a SAMEKH follows immediately (single-witness), disclosed as paragraph texture rather than a row-final close, because 26:19 reopens the same messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה…", oshb:Ezek.26.19) against the SAME 2fs addressee (Tyre), so no addressee-class shift separates 26:15-18 from 26:19-21 and the mark alone does not license a cut here; that seam is disclosed as paragraph-grade. Close (both sides): 26:21 ends "בַּלָּה֥וֹת אֶתְּנֵ֖ךְ וְאֵינֵ֑ךְ וּֽתְבֻקְשִׁ֗י וְלֹֽא תִמָּצְאִ֥י עוֹד֙ לְעוֹלָ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.21), the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH formula, with a SAMEKH immediately after (single-witness) — closing the whole Ezek.26 Tyre-siege chapter before 27:1 opens a fresh strict word-event onset for the qinah proper. Behind this row, 26:14 closed the siege-detail unit on the stacked "I YHWH have spoken" + utterance formulas and a SAMEKH (single-witness).
P06-007.device_notes: No K/Q or editorial note falls inside 26:15-21. The two paseq sites in this chapter (26:15, 26:16) are disclosed as count-only, single-witness. The 26:18 SAMEKH is disclosed as single-witness evidence with no text-formula corroboration on its own, and is treated as paragraph texture rather than a row-final close because 26:19 reopens against the same addressee. This chapter divides into four messenger units and whether the third and fourth stand apart is a held question; this row keeps them together. The 26:18/26:19 seam is paragraph-grade: 26:19's messenger formula changes no addressee, 26:18 ends on no close-role formula, and the samekh recorded on 26:18 (single-witness) corroborates a paragraph and decides nothing. That held question, not the mark, is what holds this row's confidence where it stands.

P08-012.boundary_rationale: Onset: a samekh follows MT 36:15 (single-witness), the paragraph mark behind this unit's onset. A fresh strict-form word-event formula crosses a hard seam at Ezek.36.16 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.36.16), the fifth such hard seam since Ezek.33.1 (33.1, 33.23, 34.1, 35.1, 36.16) and not the last — 37.15 and 38.1 follow. 'Son of man' at Ezek.36.17 בֶּן אָדָ֗ם בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשְׁבִ֣ים עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם וַיְטַמְּא֣וּ אוֹתָ֔הּ בְּדַרְכָּ֖ם וּבַעֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם כְּטֻמְאַת֙ הַנִּדָּ֔ה הָיְתָ֥ה דַרְכָּ֖ם לְפָנָֽי (oshb:Ezek.36.17) opens a retrospective on Israel's own defilement of the land and the resulting exile — a distinct tense and topic from the 'mountains of Israel' address just closed. Inside the span a samekh follows MT 36:21 (single-witness); the unit does not cut there because the messenger-formula pivot at Ezek.36.22 לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר לְבֵֽית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לֹ֧א לְמַעַנְכֶ֛ם אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י אִם לְשֵׁם קָדְשִׁי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֔ם בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אתֶם שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.36.22) (“I don’t do this for your sake” (web:Ezek.36.22)) opens with a 'therefore' consequence-clause: it draws out the result of the profanation narrated in the third person at Ezek.36.20 וַיָּב֗וֹא אֶל הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔ם וַֽיְחַלְּל֖וּ אֶת שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י בֶּאֱמֹ֤ר לָהֶם֙ עַם יְהוָ֣ה אֵ֔לֶּה וּמֵאַרְצ֖וֹ יָצָֽאוּ (oshb:Ezek.36.20) and Ezek.36.21 וָאֶחְמֹ֖ל עַל שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י אֲשֶׁ֤ר חִלְּל֨וּהוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁמָּה (oshb:Ezek.36.21), where 'my holy name' is twice named as the thing profaned, and the same holy-name argument runs from there through 36.22 to the utterance close at 36.23. The turn from third-person narration to second-person address at 36.22 is disclosed here as a sub-onset within that one argument, not as an addressee change that would cut the unit. Close: the utterance formula at Ezek.36.23 וְקִדַּשְׁתִּ֞י אֶת שְׁמִ֣י הַגָּד֗וֹל הַֽמְחֻלָּל֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֖ם בְּתוֹכָ֑ם וְיָדְע֨וּ הַגּוֹיִ֜ם כִּי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה בְּהִקָּדְשִׁ֥י בָכֶ֖ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.36.23), whose own bytes carry, immediately before the utterance formula, a recognition clause addressed to the nations, one of the 64 such verses book-wide and refrain-grade in class. Both that clause and the utterance signature stand mid-verse: the verse runs on after נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה with a dependent temporal infinitive, and no mark is recorded on it (single-witness). Its far face, 36.24, opens on no particle of any tracked class, belongs to no device class and carries no mark (single-witness; oshb:Ezek.36.24); the seam therefore rests on its near face alone. On a strict verse-final test that close is mid-verse; read with its dependent completion, a recognition clause and an utterance signature followed by nothing but a temporal infinitive, it stands as an ordinary licensed close, and that disclosed reading of the near face is what this row's boundary evidence records.
P08-012.device_notes: One announcement of salvation runs across 36.16-38 as a single unit; this row and the two after it subdivide that span at its own internal refrain-grade closes (disclosed once here). The cross-tradition question on 36.23-38 (the differently ordered Greek witness in this stretch) is named here as METADATA ONLY — it is not boundary evidence, not a seam.
P08-012.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the gather/cleanse/new-heart material of 36.24-32 as one continuous oracle of salvation. Rejected because the recognition-plus-utterance material of oshb:Ezek.36.23 runs from the major disjunctive through to the verse's last word, its formula tokens standing mid-verse with only a dependent temporal infinitive (בְּהִקָּדְשִׁ֥י בָכֶ֖ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם, oshb:Ezek.36.23; WLC/OSHB, single witness) after them, which grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal and not the weak mid-verse shape, and oshb:Ezek.36.24 opens the actual return and renewal rather than continuing 36.16-23's retrospective argument about the profaned name — no particle stands there in the Hebrew, and the English version's ‘For’ is translation wording that argues no boundary. That both resulting rows then sit inside the 7-10 verse band is disclosed and argues nothing.

P10-014.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:13 opens with an explicit topic header, וְאֵ֨לֶּה מִדּ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ (oshb:Ezek.43.13), the vav-initial “These are the measurements of the altar” (web:Ezek.43.13), functioning as a list-onset in the same way such headers do elsewhere in the book, immediately after the doubled inclusio that closes 43:12. The row descends through the altar's base, lower and greater ledges, hearth and horns, in cubit-and-handbreadth units, one of which (43:15) carries two OSHB editors' notes, one marking an anomalous form and one recording a ketiv/qere decision the editors take with the Leningrad Codex against BHS, while the span's one K/Q note stands at 43:16. What the confidence this row carries rests on is that pairing at each seam: the altar list's own heading at 43:13 - a discourse turn carrying no formula - against the colophon that closes the torah of the house at 43:12 (oshb:Ezek.43.12), and a content close at 43:17 against the licensed speech at 43:18 (oshb:Ezek.43.18); the measuring survey does not extend to this span; and the division of this material is a held question, which caps the confidence at the level this row carries, no bespoke ground for less being stated here.
P10-014.device_notes: No parashah mark falls in this row (single-witness). One K/Q verse is disclosed: 43:16 carries a K/Q note on the altar-hearth term, whose ketiv stands unpointed in the running text. 43:15 carries no K/Q note; its two editors' notes mark an anomalous form and record a ketiv/qere decision taken with the Leningrad Codex against BHS. The disputed reading at 43:16 is the lexical noun itself, not a numeral, so no measurement digit in this row is under dispute even though that verse sits directly beside cubit figures. No paseq touches 43:13-43:17 (single-witness).
P10-014.strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 43:13-17 with the ordinance row that follows (43:18-27) was weighed and rejected: 43:18 opens with the speech to the prophet, 'son of man' plus the messenger formula, a licensed onset inside the vision opening a law unit distinct from the altar's bare measurements.

P11-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.44.1, a counted member of the transport class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), opens with a returning-transport verb that reopens the vision frame after the utterance close and double samekh at Ezek.43.27. The prophet is shown the shut east gate and told its meaning (44.2), with the prince's privilege attached (44.3); 44.4 carries a further transport verb (a fresh entry by the north gate) and closes with the prostration formula “I fell on my face” (web:Ezek.44.4), matching the vision's own inclusio elsewhere, the same English wording standing at 1.28, 3.23, 9.8 and 43.3. Close: the prostration at 44.4 is weighed against the immediately following verse, Ezek.44.5, which opens with a fresh son-of-man address and a directive to mark, see and hear the house's ordinances -- a class shift from vision narrative to statute. Both sides of the seam are text-signalled: the vision's own close-device on one side, a fresh address opening a distinct instructional mode on the other.
P11-001.device_notes: MT 44.3 carries an OSHB 'anomalous form' editorial note and a second editors' note recording a ketiv/qere decision relative to BHS (single-witness apparatus), both disclosed and not argued as boundary evidence. MEASURED in this witness, which records a mark ON the verse it FOLLOWS: two consecutive samekh marks stand on Ezek.43.27 (single-witness), the verse immediately before this row's first verse, so those marks stand behind the span rather than inside it; no mark stands on Ezek.44.1-Ezek.44.4 (single-witness); and the next mark in the book is the pe on Ezek.44.14 (single-witness), well beyond this close. Each mark corroborates only and never decides a seam alone. The close is weighed against the alternative close at 44.3, the shut gate alone, and rests on the transport-and-prostration close at 44.4. The speech to the prophet at 44.2 is a licensed onset wherever it stands inside a vision; it is weighed as a rival at 44.1/44.2 and held, since it gives the shut gate the transport has just reached its meaning and a cut there would leave a one-verse remainder behind.

P11-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: a transport verb at Ezek.47.1 (“He brought me back to the door of the temple” (web:Ezek.47.1)) continues the vision after the hard seam at 46.24/47.1; a second transport verb follows immediately at 47.2, then the measuring sequence proper (3-5, four successive measured wadings) -- disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation from a pure vision report, since the passage briefly carries the measuring survey's own device before returning to vision narrative. The row covers the river's rise from the threshold (1-2), the four measured wadings (3-5), the 'have you seen, son of man' address (6) and the return to the bank, the riverside trees and the healed sea (7-10), the unhealed swamps (11, a K/Q verse), and the closing description of the riverbank trees bearing monthly fruit (12), where the construction glossed 'its months' is disclosed as the book's final chodesh-root homograph, not a date formula. Close: 47.12 ends in description - the riverbank trees bearing fruit month by month - with no close formula of any kind, and the samekh recorded on Ezek.47.12 (single-witness) corroborates without deciding; the next verse, 47.13, opens with a fresh messenger formula addressed to the land-division topic -- a genre shift from vision to statute/allotment, the hard seam at 47.12/47.13. A descriptive close carrying no formula on the near face is the ground of the confidence this row records.
P11-010.device_notes: Category deviation, disclosed: this row's span briefly carries the measuring survey's own device (the four measured wadings, 47.3-5) inside what is otherwise a plain vision report; disclosed in this one sentence rather than split into a separate row, since no formula bounds 47.3-5 off on either side. The two transport verses inside that circuit were weighed as rival onsets and not taken. A seam at 47.2/47.3 would strand 47.1-2 as a two-verse row, and a row that short is held only for a complete word-event unit, which those two verses are not; a seam at 47.3/47.4 would part the second measuring of a thousand from the one before it. Neither far face carries a close formula or a mark (single-witness), 47.2 ending on water trickling from the right-hand side and 47.3 on ankle-deep water, and in neither candidate does the guided-motion form open the verse, 47.3 opening on the man's going out and 47.4 on the measure verb, so both rivals are one-faced and weaker than the 47.5/47.6 rival. K/Q notes fall at Ezek.47.8, 47.10, 47.11 and 47.12 inside this row -- a locally dense cluster -- disclosed as textual-variant sites; no boundary is argued from any of them. Ezek.47.12 carries the construction glossed 'its months', the last of the book's chodesh-root homographs, disclosed as NOT a date formula. Paseq is recorded within Ezek.47.9 (one) and Ezek.47.12 (two), count-only, single-witness. Inside the span, Ezek.47.8 opens with the speech to the prophet (oshb:Ezek.47.8), a licensed onset wherever it stands inside a vision; it is weighed and not taken, because that speech interprets the river just measured and keeps the prophet within the one scene.
P11-010.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 47.5/47.6 to isolate the measuring circuit (47.3-5) as its own temple_measurement row. It is weighed and held on stated grounds. The rival's near face, Ezek.47.6, IS licensed: the verse is both a said-to-me verse and a guided-motion verse (וַיּוֹלִכֵ֥נִי, וַיְשִׁבֵ֖נִי), and it is a transport verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses), so a seam there would not be device-free. Its far face, Ezek.47.5, carries the fourth measure-verb occurrence and a content close (נַ֖חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יֵעָבֵֽר), with no close-role formula and no parashah mark (single-witness), so the rival is one-faced rather than two-faced. The row holds against it on three stated grounds: Ezek.47.6's question looks BACK at the measuring just reported and its motion returns the prophet to the bank inside one scene rather than opening a new one; the river vision runs 47:1-12 as one measured circuit with 47:6 inside it as interior texture; and the only further signal at 47:6 is the English version's mid-verse paragraph, a feature of that version's own layout which never corroborates a seam. Guided-motion verbs stand inside the measuring circuit, though not at its head: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, Ezek.47.3 does not BEGIN with a guided-motion verb (it opens בְּצֵאת הָאִ֥ישׁ) but does carry וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי later in the verse, and Ezek.47.4 carries that same form twice. Both verses are members of the same counted class, standing inside the measuring circuit, weighed and not taken, since each of those verbs steps the prophet one wading further after a measuring of a thousand cubits rather than opening a new scene. The measuring sequence therefore remains texture inside the single river vision running 47.1-12, disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation rather than split into a separate row (oshb:Ezek.47.5, oshb:Ezek.47.3, oshb:Ezek.47.6).

The phrase בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י (oshb:Ezek.2.5) ('rebellious house') recurs at 2:5, inside the same address whose close at 2:7 echoes it. The samekh after oshb:Ezek.1.28 closes the preceding unit's own vision scene and is not this unit's onset evidence. A licensed rival stands inside the row at 2:2/2:3: 2:3 opens וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.2.3), one of the said-to-me verses that carry an onset inside a vision, and the pe recorded on 2:2 is entered as corroboration for that rival rather than for the row. It is weighed and not taken, because a cut there would leave 2:1-2, two verses that are no complete word-event unit, and because the sending speech at 2:3 addresses the same hearer the commission opened with at 2:1.
P01-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through 2:10. Rejected because the pe recorded after 2:7 (single-witness) and the fresh scroll material that begins at 2:8 part the address from what follows, so that material belongs to the following unit rather than this one; 2:7 itself ends on no counted close formula, so the seam is argued from that paragraph mark and the content turn rather than from a refrain.

No K/Q note and no paseq falls anywhere in 8:14-18; that samekh is the only Masoretic item this witness records in the span (single-witness). The cry in the prophet's ears runs across this close: 8:18 carries וְקָרְא֤וּ בְאָזְנַי֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל (oshb:Ezek.8.18) as the clause before its last, and oshb:Ezek.9.1 opens וַיִּקְרָ֣א בְאָזְנַ֗י ק֤וֹל גָּדוֹל֙ with the same loud-voice wording, disclosed as a catchword straddling the seam and offered as evidence for neither side of it. Neither is taken: 8:15 only points forward to what 8:16 then shows and 8:17 puts the same question to the same tableau, so each carries the tour on instead of opening a unit, and a cut at either would leave a row under three verses that is no complete word-event unit.
P02-003.strongest_rejected_alternative: The live rival is a seam at 8:15/8:16, weighed here face by face and held. Its far face is the pointer close at oshb:Ezek.8.15, the third of this tour's forward-pointing 'you will again see' transitions (8:6, 8:13, 8:15); its near face, the candidate onset, is oshb:Ezek.8.16, a transport verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses) and one of this vision's scene seams: this witness carries a said-to-me verse at 8:5 and transports at 8:7, 8:14 and 8:16. The rival is therefore licensed on its near face and one-faced, and it is not dismissed. The row holds because a licensed driver yields a row under three verses only when it is a complete word-event unit: a cut before 8:16 leaves 8:14-8:15, which MEASURED on the WEB face is only 2 verses (the remainder 8:16-8:18 has 3) and is not a complete word-event unit. The samekh recorded on MT 8:14 (single-witness) is entered as support for the alternative it favours and no wider: a mark is recorded on the verse it stands after, so honouring it as a close would end this row at its own onset verse, 8:14, a one-verse row that is no complete word-event unit, and a section break carries corroborating weight only, ranking below every licensed driver.

P02-007.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.10.18 וַיֵּצֵא֙ כְּב֣וֹד יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן הַבָּ֑יִת וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד עַל הַכְּרוּבִֽים resumes narrated action — כבוד יהוה goes out from the threshold and stands over the cherubim, the second stage of the glory's departure begun at 10:4. Close: oshb:Ezek.10.22 וּדְמ֣וּת פְּנֵיהֶ֔ם הֵ֣מָּה הַפָּנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָאִ֨יתִי֙ עַל נְהַר כְּבָ֔ר מַרְאֵיהֶ֖ם וְאוֹתָ֑ם אִ֛ישׁ אֶל עֵ֥בֶר פָּנָ֖יו יֵלֵֽכוּ completes the 'river Chebar' identification “the faces which I saw by the river Chebar … They each went straight forward.” (web:Ezek.10.22), immediately before oshb:Ezek.11.1 opens a fresh transport (“the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate” (web:Ezek.11.1)) that continues from the very place — the east gate — where 10:19 had just stood the cherubim. Both sides: the onset is corroborated by the counted glory-movement device (sweep: 9 verses); the close has no parashah mark (chapter 10 carries none) but is corroborated by the double Chebar citation at 10:20 and 10:22 and by the clean handoff to 11:1's transport verb, which is the strongest close-side evidence available in this mark-free chapter.

P02-012.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.12.8 וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י בַּבֹּ֥קֶר לֵאמֹֽר — the word-event re-onset that infixes בַּבֹּ֥קֶר (oshb:Ezek.12.8), 'in the morning' (one of 41 verses carrying the vayehi-form word-event, and one of only two in the book that infix a phrase before לֵאמֹֽר, the other being the dateline at oshb:Ezek.24.1) — opens the interpretation of the sign-act just performed. P02-017.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.13.10 יַ֣עַן וּבְיַ֜עַן הִטְע֧וּ אֶת עַמִּ֛י לֵאמֹ֥ר שָׁל֖וֹם וְאֵ֣ין שָׁל֑וֹם וְהוּא֙ בֹּ֣נֶה חַ֔יִץ וְהִנָּ֛ם טָחִ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ תָּפֵֽל turns to the whitewash-wall metaphor “Because, even because they have seduced my people, saying, … and there is no peace.” (web:Ezek.13.10), with a fresh messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.13.13. Close: oshb:Ezek.13.16 נְבִיאֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַֽנִבְּאִים֙ אֶל יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְהַחֹזִ֥ים לָ֖הּ חֲז֣וֹן שָׁלֹ֑ם וְאֵ֣ין שָׁלֹ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה, naming “the prophets of Israel who prophesy concerning Jerusalem… visions of peace… and there is no peace” (web:Ezek.13.16); a pe follows this verse (single-witness), and an OSHB editorial note (single-witness apparatus) also falls here. Both sides: the onset continues the indictment the strict word-event at oshb:Ezek.13.1 opens, without an addressee change, so its near face at 13:10 is a turn in the argument that carries no counted formula, and that near face is what keeps this row's confidence down; the messenger-formula-plus-utterance-close bracket at the far end is clean and corroborated by the pe recorded on this row's last verse.
P02-017.device_notes: Editorial note and pe both fall at oshb:Ezek.13.16, disclosed above; the note is a single-witness apparatus remark and is not read as touching the verse's byte content. Paseq at oshb:Ezek.13.11 is count-only, single-witness. The judgement speech that the messenger formula opens (13:13-14) ends on the recognition refrain in its second-person-plural form (sweep: 21 verses), and the verse that carries it also belongs to the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), so refrain-grade close evidence stands inside this row. A seam after that refrain was weighed and not taken: the coda (13:15-16) opens on a plain continuation verb in no counted class, no mark follows the refrain verse (single-witness), and the two-verse coda would be a row under three verses that is not a complete word-event unit.
P02-017.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 13:1-16 as one sixteen-verse row (no split at 13:10) was weighed, since the same prophets remain the addressee throughout. It was not taken because splitting at the image change — from the foxes-and-walls accusation to the whitewash metaphor proper, with its own messenger formula at 13:13 — is the ground; that both halves then sit inside the 7-10 verse target is disclosed, not argued.

P03-016.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:10 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְהוֹלִ֥יד בֵּן פָּרִ֖יץ שֹׁפֵ֣ךְ דָּ֑ם וְעָ֣שָׂה אָ֔ח מֵאַחַ֖ד מֵאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Ezek.18.10) ('and he fathers a violent son who sheds blood'), continuing the case-law series by default. The seam behind this onset is the one interior seam of the unit whose formula stands verse-final: 18:9 ends on the utterance signature, verse-final and unmarked, but 18:10 brings no fresh onset past it, so that signature is paragraph-final and not a unit close. The righteous grandson's case (18:14) and the summary restatement (18:19-20) follow without any fresh formula onset of their own, since 18:18 explicitly recalls the father's own guilt from 18:10-13 before drawing the general rule -- one continuous legal argument across three generations, not three independently onset units. Close side: the row runs through 18:20; its opening clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא יִשָּׂ֣א בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב (oshb:Ezek.18.20) ('the soul who sins shall die; a son shall not bear his father's iniquity') restates 18:4's thesis and closes the argument, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse (single-witness). Both of this row's seams are case turns inside one word-event unit, with no formula on the near face of either: 18:21 opens the repentance case past the close with none of its own, and the samekh recorded on 18:20 corroborates that close without deciding it. That pair of seams is the ground on which this row is held at reduced confidence.

P04-012.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.20.27 opens לָכֵ֞ן דַּבֵּ֨ר אֶל בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (oshb:Ezek.20.27), a therefore-command to the hearers this speech has already addressed, so its near face carries an onset-class device that nothing here licenses. Behind it oshb:Ezek.20.26 ends לְמַ֨עַן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֵֽדְע֔וּ אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.20.26), a recognition-shaped clause in the asher form that the counted list does not hold, and a samekh is recorded on that verse (single-witness), corroborating the paragraph and deciding nothing. Close: oshb:Ezek.20.38 ends וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.20.38), the recognition family's 2mp form standing verse-final and counted, and across the seam oshb:Ezek.20.39 opens וְאַתֶּ֨ם בֵּֽית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר (oshb:Ezek.20.39), an address licensed by that verse-final close, so the close seam is two-faced. Interior: the 20:29/20:30 pair carries no formula and no mark on either face, and oshb:Ezek.20.30 renews at לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Ezek.20.30) the command oshb:Ezek.20.27 has already given to the same hearers, so it is paragraph-grade and weighed rather than taken. An onset near face that carries an unlicensed device, with nothing counted across the seam behind it, is the ground on which this row is held at reduced confidence, whatever its close seam carries.
P04-012.device_notes: No parashah mark stands anywhere inside 20:27-20:38; the samekh recorded on oshb:Ezek.20.26 (single-witness) sits behind the onset, on the verse immediately before it. Paseq, count-only and single-witness, stands at oshb:Ezek.20.30 and at oshb:Ezek.20.32; where each stroke sits inside its verse is not recoverable from this witness's verse text. No K/Q note falls in the span. The as-I-live oath at oshb:Ezek.20.31 reinforces the indictment and the oath-plus-utterance at oshb:Ezek.20.33 is paragraph-internal; neither is read as a seam. The close at oshb:Ezek.20.38 belongs to the wider recognition-family idiom in its 2mp form (sweep: 21 verses) and not to the strict 28-verse recognition list, and the two counts are never blended.
P04-012.literature_type_guess: renewed indictment of the fathers: the Bamah aetiology, the oath to reign, and the wilderness purge
P04-012.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this span back into the disputation that opens at oshb:Ezek.20.1 would dissolve this row's own onset seam at 20:26/20:27 and propose no interior cut. It is weighed and declined: the therefore-command at oshb:Ezek.20.27 turns the speech from the wilderness retrospective to a fresh indictment of the hearers, the samekh recorded on oshb:Ezek.20.26 (single-witness) stands with that turn without deciding it, and the close at oshb:Ezek.20.38 is counted and verse-final, so the material of 20:27-20:38 is bracketed in its own right. A second cut at the embedded oath and utterance of oshb:Ezek.20.33 was also weighed and declined: no fresh onset-class device follows it, so a mid-unit utterance closes a paragraph, not a row.

P06-006.boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:7 reopens with the messenger formula, "כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֧ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֛ל מִצָּפ֖וֹן מֶ֣לֶךְ מְלָכִ֑ים בְּס֛וּס וּבְרֶ֥כֶב וּבְפָרָשִׁ֖ים וְקָהָ֥ל וְעַם רָֽב" (oshb:Ezek.26.7), introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege by name — a fresh speech unit following the 26:6 close. In the WEB, “For the Lord Yahweh says: ‘Behold, I will bring on Tyre Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, from the north, with horses, with chariots, with horsemen, and an army with many people.” (web:Ezek.26.7). Close (both sides): 26:14 ends "וּנְתַתִּ֞יךְ לִצְחִ֣יחַ סֶ֗לַע מִשְׁטַ֤ח חֲרָמִים֙ תִּֽהְיֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִבָּנֶ֖ה ע֑וֹד כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.14), stacking TWO closes in one verse — "for I YHWH have spoken" (the 14-verse emphatic-close family) and the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature (the 81-verse family) — with a samekh immediately after (single-witness). How chapter 26 divides - one row for each of its four messenger units, or fewer - is an open question here, and that question, not these faces, is what holds this row at reduced confidence, on the same reading the preceding unit of the chapter carries. Behind, 26:6 closed the first unit on the recognition formula with a pe recorded on that verse (single-witness); ahead, 26:15 reopens with a further fresh messenger formula shifting from direct 2fs address of Tyre's destruction to the scene of the sea-princes' reaction.
P06-006.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 26:18, which would bring the span nearer the 7-10 verse target, was rejected: 26:14 carries two stacked close formulas with a samekh recorded on that verse (single-witness), and 26:15 opens with its own messenger formula on a distinct scene (the princes' mourning), so folding it in would submerge an independently marked close.

P08-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: 36:24 opens on a plain weqatal, וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ מִן הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְקִבַּצְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִכָּל הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל אַדְמַתְכֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.36.24) - no particle and no counted device stands at its head, and the English 'For' is the translation's connective rather than anything this witness carries - continuing the shared Ezek.36.16 word-event frame (disclosed, verse-anchored) and opening the gather-and-return material. Sprinkling and cleansing follow at Ezek.36.25, then MT 36.26 reads וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָכֶם֙ לֵ֣ב חָדָ֔שׁ וְר֥וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וַהֲסִ֨רֹתִ֜י אֶת לֵ֤ב הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מִבְּשַׂרְכֶ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָכֶ֖ם לֵ֥ב בָּשָֽׂר (oshb:Ezek.36.26), reading 'a new heart', spliced directly from this witness, in explicit contrast with MT 11.19, which in this same witness reads וְנָתַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ לֵ֣ב אֶחָ֔ד וְר֥וּחַ חֲדָשָׁ֖ה אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֑ם וַהֲסִ֨רֹתִ֜י לֵ֤ב הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מִבְּשָׂרָ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָהֶ֖ם לֵ֥ב בָּשָֽׂר (oshb:Ezek.11.19), reading “one heart” (web:Ezek.11.19) (with 'a new spirit' as the item that is new there): Ezek.11.19 is not a 'new heart' verse in WLC/OSHB, though the wider manuscript and versional tradition often reads it that way; this observation is scoped to this single witness and claims nothing about that wider tradition. P10-005.boundary_rationale: Onset side: this seam carries no formula evidence of its own. 40:38 opens וְלִשְׁכָּ֣ה וּפִתְחָ֔הּ בְּאֵילִ֖ים הַשְּׁעָרִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.40.38), “A room with its door was by the posts at the gates” (web:Ezek.40.38), with a bare vav, no transport verb and no measuring verb -- the topic shifts from gate architecture to the functional furniture used for slaughtering and washing the sacrifices, but nothing in the bytes marks the shift as a formula onset; it rests on content alone, following directly on the north inner gate's close at 40:37. The row continues through the singers' and priests' chambers (40:44-46, including the Zadokite priestly qualification, case-law texture inside a measurement row, disclosed) and closes at 40:47's וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.40.47) “The altar was before the house” (web:Ezek.40.47), a summary notice before 40:48's transport verb moves the tour into the temple building itself. Both sides of this row are held to a lower confidence than its neighbors precisely because neither its onset nor its close carries a counted formula device.
P10-005.device_notes: No parashah, K/Q or editorial note touches 40:38-40:47. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: two occurrences (40:43, 40:47). Content disclosure, not a category deviation: 40:44-46 carries priestly-qualification (Zadokite) texture that reads closer to temple law than to the measurement category; the row is classed as measurement because dimensioned description dominates it (tables, hooks, court) and the qualification clause is two verses inside a ten-verse row. P10-011.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:15 opens וְכִלָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.15) “when he had finished measuring the inner house” (web:Ezek.42.15) -- a completion notice, not a counted formula, pressed into onset service here, since it explicitly marks the end of the inner-house survey that has run since 40:5 before turning outward to the perimeter wall -- paired with the transport verb וְהוֹצִיאַ֨נִי֙ 'he brought me out', which makes 42:15 a verse of the counted guided-motion class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences) and gives the onset a licensed driver inside the vision. Four cardinal-direction measurements follow (east 42:16, north 42:17, south 42:18, west 42:19), each carrying its own measure verb, verse-initial at 42:16 and 42:17 and after the direction word at 42:18 and 42:19, then a summary at 42:20. Close side: 42:20 ends on the wall's purpose, לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹֽל (oshb:Ezek.42.20) “to make a separation between that which was holy and that which was common” (web:Ezek.42.20) -- a genuine thematic close, and the point at which the whole measuring circuit that opened at 40:5 ends, immediately before 43:1's transport verb and the glory's return open a new kind of scene. Both sides of this seam are unusually well aligned: a completion-formula onset and a purpose-clause close on one side, a transport-plus-glory onset on the other.
P10-011.device_notes: No parashah mark stands anywhere in chapter 42 (single-witness); the first mark after the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29 is the samekh recorded on 43:9, so this seam has no Masoretic paragraph corroboration of its own. One K/Q verse disclosed (42:16): the ketiv reads cubits where the qere reads hundreds, so the disputed word is the multiplier of the reed count itself, a numeral; no boundary is argued from it. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: two occurrences (42:15, 42:20); where each stands within its verse is not recoverable from the verse text of the witness.
